data.subject: Direction v4: panel-layer estimation, five-sleeve holding, cost-gated net-CNY account
data.decision: Adopt direction v4 and design v10 as the working plan, provisionally: estimation moves to the A-share panel, holding stays at five ETF sleeves rebalanced at most monthly, the interface is a per-sleeve (mu, sigma, es) vector combined by a rule with at most four fitted parameters, and the only evidence that counts is net CNY in the append-only ledger plus a forward paper book.
data.rationale: Three rounds narrowed the direction twice and blocked it on five highs plus one medium. Two of those are answerable by construction rather than by hope: the 27% ceiling becomes a VaR construction plus a drawdown throttle plus a rejection rule (F-113a8e8d-4), and panel-layer training removes the 900-row parameter cap while withdrawing the 'trivial CPU' scale claim (F-113a8e8d-5). The remaining four are answerable only by measurement, and design v10 names each measurement and its pre-declared rule: block-bootstrap uncertainty plus a sleeve-deviation share threshold (F-113a8e8d-1), ridge versus MLP on identical features routed through the same account engine (F-113a8e8d-2), the claim narrowed to a complexity benchmark at this sample (F-113a8e8d-3), and executable-month plus FIXED counts reported per fold (F-113a8e8d-6). Because four objections remain open until E1 reports, the direction is recorded provisional rather than adopted: the build steps that do not depend on the model question (frozen inputs, ledger, invariants, feasibility report) proceed now, and the prediction branch ships only under E1's rule.
data.applicability: Holds for a CN A-share ETF account of 50,000-100,000 CNY with five sleeves, board lot 100, commission 0.00025 floored at 5 CNY per non-zero order, ETF stamp duty 0, transfer 1e-05, one-way slippage 5bp assumed (not measured). Says nothing about accounts large enough that the fixed 5 CNY is a few basis points of a slice.
data.verifyPlan: Build steps 1-4 produce a frozen instrument table, an ETF panel, a ledger whose replay hash is stable, and a feasibility report quoting executable months at 50k/75k/100k. If the feasibility report shows fewer than half of months have any gate-clearing order, direction v4's premise fails before E1 is even run and this decision is reopened.
data.reopenCondition: E1 returns null under its three-part rule (prediction branch closes, project re-scopes to account infrastructure), or the feasibility report shows under 50% executable months, or the measured one-way spread differs from the assumed 5bp by more than 2x.
data.override: Four high objections (F-113a8e8d-1, -2, -3, -6) stay open until E1 runs. The override is scoped: only the model-independent build steps are authorized to proceed, and no candidate ships, no baseline is retired, and nothing is counted as answered until E1 reports against its preregistered rule.

data.subject: The 27% drawdown ceiling is a construction plus a rejection rule, never a realised-drawdown check
data.decision: Define the drawdown mandate in three parts, all inside the allocator or the evaluator, none inferred after the fact: ex-ante, target weights are chosen so the book's 1-month 95% VaR is at most d_max/6, so six consecutive worst months reach the ceiling before rebalance evidence arrives; a state throttle halves the equity target whenever book drawdown from running peak exceeds d_max/2, restoring at recovery; and any walk-forward or paper path whose running drawdown exceeds d_max is rejected regardless of return.
data.rationale: The objection was correct: a realised-drawdown check cannot enforce a prospective ceiling under monthly trading with gaps, because it measures what happened rather than bounding what can happen. A VaR-scaled construction bounds the loss per month before the trade; six such months are the arithmetic budget for the ceiling; the throttle handles the path where the VaR model itself is wrong. The rejection rule keeps the mandate binding even when the construction fails, which is the only honest arrangement.
data.applicability: Holds while the mandate is expressed as a maximum drawdown on the total book including cash, and while monthly returns are the decision frequency so that one month is the smallest bet of size. It does not bound intra-month gaps: a single-day move larger than the monthly VaR estimate is outside this construction.
data.verifyPlan: In the three-arm replay, count the fraction of walk-forward paths whose running drawdown exceeds d_max. Zero exceedances across folds supports the construction; any exceedance reopens it and forces the coarse 20-28% bond block fallback with reported tracking error.
data.reopenCondition: Any fold or paper-book month where running drawdown exceeds d_max, or where the monthly VaR estimate is breached by more than 2x in a single month.
data.override: Recorded adopted although F-113a8e8d-4 stays listed open, because the objection asks for a construction or an evaluation rule and this supplies both; whether the construction actually bounds anything is a separate empirical claim tested by the walk-forward path count, not by this decision.

data.subject: Band-rule line closed; its four remaining objections retired by scope and by the ETF stamp-duty correction
data.decision: Retire the four remaining band-rule objections; the band rule survives only as a reported sensitivity and cannot set a shipped rule
data.rationale: Each of the four objections presupposes a shipped band rule. F-60b5f78a-1 asked the band to demonstrate it compensates for exposure drift and F-60b5f78a-3 asked for measured risk evidence behind a granularity census; both become non-binding once the band is a reported sensitivity and the default arm is static, because a reported number cannot set the shipped rule. F-60b5f78a-5 (the livelock) was the arithmetic proof that demoted the band in the first place, so it is the reason for the decision rather than an open charge against it. F-60b5f78a-4 and -6 (stamp duty) are closed by correcting the instrument fact: ETF stamp duty is zero, the 0.0005 rate is a stock rate, and the goal text inherited it by mistake. F-60b5f78a-7 (dividends and splits) is closed structurally: corporate actions are now a layer-0 input and invariant I-5 makes the ex-date cash change a test rather than an assumption.
data.verifyPlan: The three-arm replay reports the band arm as a sensitivity column whose numbers never enter the shipped rule; a test asserts the shipped weight function does not read the band parameter.
data.reopenCondition: Capital changes by five times, or the measured one-way spread falls near 1-2bp so that the annual trading budget rises above a hurdle a policy could plausibly capture.

data.subject: E1 adoption rule: folded majority, 90% moving-block bootstrap CI excluding zero, and at least 375 CNY/yr at 75,000 CNY
data.decision: E1 preregistration: nonlinearity is adopted at the panel layer only if it beats a same-feature ridge on net CNY under a three-part rule fixed before the first fold is read
data.rationale: The comparison has to be one-variable at the decision level or its result cannot be attributed: identical frozen features, identical walk-forward folds, identical aggregation, identical cost gate and account engine, differing only in ridge versus MLP at the panel layer. The primary measure is net CNY at 75,000 CNY rather than IC, because P2 is the standing evidence that rank IC and money point in different directions. Three thresholds are required together so that a marginal win cannot be promoted: a fold majority, a dependence-preserving interval, and an economic size above the annual trading budget scale. The block bootstrap resamples six-month blocks of calendar dates, which preserves both autocorrelation and cross-sleeve correlation, the two dependence structures that make a naive month-wise interval too narrow.
data.remainingRisk: The 4-parameter combiner may throw away interaction information the panel model carries, in which case E1 understates any nonlinearity; the guard is a combiner basis fixed before the run (expected return, expected vol, expected shortfall, deviation-from-common) and reported scores at sleeve level even where the account cannot trade them.
data.verifyPlan: The run record carries this rule verbatim in its decisionRule field; any deviation between the recorded rule and the executed comparison invalidates the run.
data.reopenCondition: A bug in the fold construction or the cost gate is found after the run, or the frozen feature set changes, either of which voids the preregistration rather than the result.

data.subject: The tradable venue is 11 instruments, not 15: four ETFs have a one-lot size that a 50-100k NAV cannot size around
data.decision: Frozen venue table: 15 ETF codes, 45,197 bars, 2013-01-04..2026-11-04, venue hash d6a6e438 (newquant/data/freeze.py -> data/venue.parquet + data/venue.manifest.json). One-lot notionals at 2026-11-04: 511010 14135, 511260 13578, 511880 10093, 511990 9999 = 13.3-28.3% of a 50k NAV (10.0-14.1% of 100k), so all four are flagged tradable=false. Cash has no usable instrument and becomes the residual balance (zero commission, T+0, no lot granularity). Bond sleeve = 511220 (1044/lot) + 511380 (1254/lot) only. Remaining tradable set = 11 codes across equity/bond/commodity/overseas.
data.rationale: A lot is indivisible, so a position whose smallest unit is >10% of NAV cannot express a sleeve weight; it can only be an all-or-nothing bet on one instrument. Holding cash in the residual balance strictly dominates a cash ETF at this capital on all three dimensions (cost, availability, granularity).
data.applicability: Holds for NAV 50k-100k CNY at 2026-11 prices with a 100-unit board lot and 5 CNY commission floor. Above ~200k NAV the 13-14k lot names become sizeable; the flag must be recomputed from the frozen price, not assumed.
data.remainingRisk: The 511220/511380 lots (1.0-2.5% of NAV) still quantise the bond sleeve to ~40-100 steps at 50-75k, so bond weight changes below ~2% of NAV are unexecutable even there. Not modelled yet.
data.verifyPlan: Recompute one_lot_pct_of_nav per code per NAV on the frozen venue table; assert the tradable set has max one-lot fraction <= 10% at every tested NAV.
data.reopenCondition: NAV above 200k, or a venue change that alters board lots or lot prices (e.g. a bond ETF split), or a broker minimum that differs from 5 CNY.

data.subject: Cost gate: 7.6 bp infimum, per-tolerance minimum order sizes, and the discreteness they force on the allocation layer
data.decision:
Subject: the cost gate has a hard 7.6 bp floor; at 50-75k the only executable policy is a small set of discrete sleeve states.

Measured from the frozen venue + fee profile (newquant/venue.py; 40 tests pass in tests/test_venue.py::TestCostArithmetic):

- One-way total rate = 5/N + var below the commission floor and commission_rate + var above it, var = transfer 1e-05 + stamp 0 + slippage 5e-04 = 0.00051. Its infimum is 7.60 bp, so NO order of any size clears T < 7.6 bp.
- Smallest clearing order per tolerance: 7.6bp -> 20,000; 10bp -> 10,204.09; 15.1bp -> 5,000.00; 30bp -> 2,008.04; 50bp -> 1,114.00; 75bp -> 716.00 CNY. Cent-ceiled then walked up a cent at a time until the same gate_ok the account uses agrees (at 50 bp the analytic 1,113.59 computes to 50.018 bp because each cost component rounds to the cent).
- As a fraction of NAV (50k/75k/100k): 10bp -> 20.4/13.6/10.2%; 15.1bp -> 10.0/6.7/5.0%; 30bp -> 4.0/2.7/2.0%.
- Against the annual-turnover cap (<=6 -> 50% of NAV per month -> 12.5% per sleeve over four investable sleeves): 10 bp is OUTSIDE the budget at 50k and 75k, 15.1 bp fits, and moves below ~7% of NAV per sleeve are unexecutable at 75k.
- Cleared (month x instrument) cells over 131 months 2016-01..2026-11: 15.1bp with a 10%-of-NAV per-sleeve move -> 0.1% at 50k, 93.9% at 75k, 99.7% at 100k; 30bp with 5% moves -> 87.8/93.9/93.9%. Shares cluster near 0% or ~94% because the gate is essentially the indicator [lot-floored notional >= N_min(T)], not a smooth function of trade size.

Consequence for L2: the allocation layer must emit a small number of discrete sleeve states (e.g. {0, 1/2, 1} of the sleeve budget), because a continuous weight would mostly be suppressed and the paper book would then measure FIXED rather than signal (F-113a8e8d-6).
data.rationale: The commission floor makes the rate curve U-shaped in N (falling then flat), so there is a strict lower bound on achievable cost rate and therefore a minimum order size for every tolerance. Computing it as a bound is not enough: the account rounds each cost component to the cent, which moves the true boundary by up to a couple of CNY, so the bound is verified against gate_ok rather than trusted.
data.remainingRisk: Slippage 5 bp is inherited from P1's matrix and NOT measured; it is 66% of the 7.6 bp floor. If measured spread were 1 bp instead of 5, the floor drops to 3.6 bp and a 10 bp tolerance would come inside budget, which would change the discreteness conclusion. This is the architecture doc's open item 10.3 and it is the single largest uncertainty in the feasibility verdict.
data.verifyPlan: Property test already in tests/test_venue.py: for tol in {7.6, 8, 10, 15.1, 30, 50, 120} the returned bound passes gate_ok and a 10%-smaller size fails; bounds are monotonically non-increasing in tolerance; tol <= 7.5 returns None.
data.reopenCondition: A measured one-way spread for these 11 ETFs (quote-level data, or realised fill-vs-mid from the paper book) replacing the assumed 5 bp, or a commission-floor change.

data.learn: E1 tells whether nonlinearity adds monthly cost-clearable information at this panel size: ridge versus MLP, identical features and folds, both routed through the same account engine, adoption only if the MLP wins >=70% of folds, has a 90% block-bootstrap CI of net difference excluding zero, and adds >=375 CNY/yr at 75,000 CNY. A null says nonlinearity is not where the money is at this sample and closes the prediction branch; it says nothing about learned predictors as a class.
data.minimalTest: Cheapest separator: fit ridge and a small MLP on the same frozen panel features for one fold, aggregate both to inclusive sleeve scores, and compare the sleeve-score rank correlation with realised next-month sleeve returns while reporting the sleeve-deviation share of score variance. If the MLP's score is indistinguishable from ridge's at the sleeve level, no account-level replay can rescue it and E1 can be shortened to the score comparison.

assumptions.claim: Monthly sleeve decisions are cost-clearable at 50k-100k only in discrete lumps, and the tradable venue is 11 instruments with cash as the residual balance: the smallest clearing order at 15.1bp is 5,000 CNY = 10.0/6.7/5.0% of a 50/75/100k NAV, at 10bp it is 10,204 CNY = 20.4/13.6/10.2% (outside the 12.5%-per-sleeve monthly budget at 50k and 75k), and the one-way rate has a hard 7.6bp floor so no order clears a tighter tolerance at any size. Four ETFs (511010, 511260, 511880, 511990) have a one-lot value of 10.0-14.1k CNY = 13.3-28.3% of a 50k NAV and are declared untradable.
assumptions.condition: Holds while commission is 0.00025 floored at 5 CNY per non-zero order, ETF stamp duty is 0, transfer 1e-05, one-way slippage 5bp (assumed, not measured), board lot 100 units, prices as frozen 2026-11-04, NAV 50k-100k.
assumptions.measure: The feasibility report (evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md) counts cleared (month x instrument) cells and FIXED sleeves; below 50% cleared cells the verdict is unmeasurable at this capital. Recompute on every venue-hash change.

cost.claim: Build to first informative result is 5-7 days of one engineer; runtime per fold is under an hour on the workstation.
cost.condition: One engineer, single Windows workstation, no paid cloud.
cost.measure: Recorded wall-clock per build step and per fold in the ledger; steps 1-4 took 1 day including the two test-driven bug fixes.

dataFlow.claim: Data flows one way from frozen inputs to evaluation, and the loop closes only at the ledger reading its own prior state.
dataFlow.condition: Holds for the five-layer layout recorded in docs/direction-architecture.md.
dataFlow.measure: A dependency test asserts no module imports upstream of itself and that only the ledger feeds back.

dataOwner.claim: The research process owns L0 artefacts and the ledger; no other module may mutate them.
dataOwner.condition: Holds while the freeze manifest and the ledger store are the only writers of their files.
dataOwner.measure: newquant/data/freeze.py is the only writer of data/venue.*, and load() raises when the parquet no longer matches its manifest hash; the ledger store is the only writer of .quant/ledger.jsonl.

failureHandling.claim: A failing order is suppressed and logged, a failing sleeve is flagged FIXED and reported, and an evaluation exceeding the mandate is rejected regardless of return.
failureHandling.condition: Holds while the cost gate and the mandate check both run before any write to the ledger.
failureHandling.measure: Suppression and FIXED counts appear in decision.json for every fold; a fold with a data gap records insufficient evidence, not a flat result.

goal.claim: Produce a net-CNY account curve at 50,000-100,000 CNY in a forward paper book whose every fee is recomputed from the venue schedule, and settle by evidence whether panel-layer nonlinearity adds cost-clearable monthly information.
goal.condition: Research and paper trading only until live trading is separately authorized.
goal.measure: Net CNY curve and per-fold cleared-cell and FIXED counts from the append-only ledger; E1's three-part adoption rule.

interface.claim: L1 exports per-sleeve mu, sigma and expected shortfall per month; L2 consumes exactly those and returns DISCRETE sleeve states (each sleeve at 0, 1/2 or 1 of its budget, with cash absorbing the residual), not continuous weights; L3 lot-rounds each state into whole units, gates the post-rounding notional, and returns fills or suppressions.
interface.condition: Holds while the sleeve_scores.parquet and order-log schemas are respected, and while the gate-clearing order size at the declared tolerance exceeds the continuous-weight increment (true at <=100k: 5,000 CNY at 15.1bp versus a 1,875 CNY increment for a 2.5% tilt of a 75k NAV).
interface.measure: Schema tests on sleeve_scores.parquet and the order log; an interface test asserts every L2 output is a member of the declared state set and that no suppressed order is silently resized.

irreversible.claim: The frozen panel and the ledger hash chain are irreversible inputs: artefacts are hashed at freeze and ledger records are append-only.
irreversible.condition: Holds while no process rewrites a frozen artefact or a sealed ledger record.
irreversible.measure: A freeze manifest with sha256 per artefact (data/venue.manifest.json, data/etf_bars.manifest.json), plus a replay test that refuses to load an edited ledger.

replaceable.claim: The model, the aggregator and the combiner are replaceable behind parquet and JSON contracts; the ledger, the instrument table and the invariants are not.
replaceable.condition: Holds while the module boundaries in docs/direction-architecture.md section 4 are respected.
replaceable.measure: Swapping ridge for MLP changes no ledger code path and no test outside the model module.

requirements.claim: Eight invariants hold as tests: NAV identity, per-fill cost recomputation, post-rounding cost gate, settlement by class, corporate actions on NAV, deterministic replay hash, sleeve combiner at most four fitted parameters, no silently suppressed sleeve.
requirements.condition: Holds for the fee schedule and settlement table recorded in the frozen venue table.
requirements.measure: 50 tests run green, and a replay of the same window produces a byte-identical ledger hash.

scale.claim: A refit is 12M panel rows by about 60 features by 13 annual folds, measured in CPU-minutes on one workstation; the sleeve combiner fits on roughly 120 months with at most four parameters over a 3-state-per-sleeve action space (3^4 = 81 admissible configurations, not a continuous simplex).
scale.condition: Single Windows workstation; the RTX 5060 is available but CPU execution is expected to suffice.
scale.measure: Reported CPU-minutes per refit in the E1 record, plus a contract test asserting the combiner parameter count and the state-set membership.

simplest.claim: Static annual rebalance of the four investable sleeves with cash as the fine stabiliser is the default arm and the baseline every candidate must beat net of cost.
simplest.condition: Holds while turnover stays at or below 6 per year, which at 50-100k is the binding budget rather than the gate.
simplest.measure: The three-arm replay decomposes cost saved versus gross exposure difference; a richer arm ships only if it beats static on net CNY.

storage.claim: L0 in parquet (bars, venue table) with a canonical-CSV sha256 in each manifest, the ledger in append-only JSONL with prev-hash chaining, evaluation outputs as CSV plus decision.json.
storage.condition: Holds while the ledger file is the single source of account state.
storage.measure: A replay test recomputes the chain head; an edited record makes the chain refuse to load, and an edited venue table makes load() raise.

validate.claim: E1's preregistered rule, the invariant suite and a forward paper book are the only validation; no in-sample score counts as evidence.
validate.condition: Holds while the E1 decision rule is written before the first fold is read.
validate.measure: The three thresholds are recorded in the ledger before the run, and the fold table is reported whether or not it passes.

data.subject: Band-rule line closed; its four remaining objections retired by scope and by the ETF stamp-duty correction
data.decision: Retire the four remaining band-rule objections; the band rule survives only as a reported sensitivity and cannot set a shipped rule
data.rationale: Same conclusion as seq 48, re-recorded with the applicability field it was missing, because without that field the state view keeps an adopted decision under hypotheses. The full argument is at seq 48 and is not restated here to avoid two divergent copies.
data.applicability: Holds for NAV 50k-100k at the frozen venue: the annual trading budget is 353 CNY/yr = 0.47% of a 50k NAV (recorded at seq 34), the one-way rate floor is now measured at 7.6 bp, and a 12-rebalance five-sleeve policy therefore pays a fixed friction that no plausible policy edge at this capital is assumed to clear. It covers the four F-60b5f78a-* objections only in so far as they presuppose a shipped band rule; a band rule promoted back into the shipped arm voids this applicability immediately.
data.remainingRisk: If the measured one-way spread turns out near 1-2 bp instead of the assumed 5 bp, the rate floor falls to 3.6 bp and the annual friction budget roughly halves, which could make a band rule worth testing rather than reporting.
data.verifyPlan: The three-arm replay reports the band arm as a sensitivity column whose numbers never enter the shipped rule; a test asserts the shipped weight function does not read the band parameter.
data.reopenCondition: Capital changes by five times, or the measured one-way spread falls near 1-2 bp so that the annual trading budget rises above a hurdle a policy could plausibly capture.

data.subject: E1 adoption rule: folded majority, 90% moving-block bootstrap CI excluding zero, and at least 375 CNY/yr at 75,000 CNY
data.decision: E1 preregistration: nonlinearity is adopted at the panel layer only if it beats a same-feature ridge on net CNY under a three-part rule fixed before the first fold is read — (i) MLP >= ridge in >= 70% of folds, (ii) the 6-month moving-block bootstrap 90% CI of the net-CNY difference excludes zero, (iii) the difference is >= 375 CNY/yr at 75,000 CNY.
data.rationale: Same rule as seq 49, re-recorded with the applicability field it was missing so the state view stops keeping an adopted preregistration under hypotheses. The full rationale is at seq 49; the three thresholds are restated verbatim here because they are the load-bearing part and must not be paraphrased.
data.applicability: Holds at monthly decision frequency with annual refit folds over 2016-2025 (10 folds), the frozen venue hash d6a6e438, and the ≤4-parameter combiner whose action space is now 3 states per sleeve over 4 investable sleeves. The 375 CNY/yr threshold is 0.5% of a 75k NAV and remains the right scale for 50k-100k; neither the fold count nor the 70% majority rule depends on the venue correction. It covers the panel-layer arms only: a change of decision frequency, of the frozen feature set, or of the cost gate voids it.
data.remainingRisk: The 4-parameter combiner may throw away interaction information the panel model carries, in which case E1 understates any nonlinearity; the guard is a combiner basis fixed before the run. Second risk: with 3 states per sleeve the arm now differs from ridge partly through discretisation, so a null could reflect the combiner rather than the model — the report must show the ridge arm's cleared-cell share alongside the net difference.
data.verifyPlan: The run record carries this rule verbatim in its decisionRule field; any deviation between the recorded rule and the executed comparison invalidates the run.
data.reopenCondition: A bug in the fold construction or the cost gate is found after the run, or the frozen feature set changes, either of which voids the preregistration rather than the result.

data.purpose: 用户要求对当前方向重新做一次 quant_review。这一轮与前三轮不同：前三轮是在没有实测数据时做的，现在 L0 冻结表、可行性报告与 50 个测试都已落地，成本门槛从假设变成实测（费率下确界 7.6bp、N_min 表、清关率 0%/94% 两簇），且设计已推到 v11（L2 接口改为离散三态）。需要判断方向本身是否仍值得做，以及贡献落在哪里。
data.question: 在 50,000–100,000 CNY 的个人 ETF 账户、月度决策、年换手 ≤6 的条件下：(1) 这个方向值得做吗——问题成立吗；(2) 贡献落在哪里：是"成本门槛决定可行动作集是离散的、估计广度与持有广度必须解耦"这个 framing 本身，还是只能落在工程与度量（把 feasibility 作为一等研究产出、"此规模不可测"作为独立结论）上；(3) 你能指出的最近前人工作是什么（请说具体，论文/章节/开源实现的位置），以及本方向与它实质差别在哪；(4) 什么样的观测会推翻这个方向——如果实测单边价差接近 1–2bp 而不是假定的 5bp，门槛降到 3.6bp，离散化结论是否随之失效，那时该方向还剩下什么。请注意一个并行的文献调查正在独立进行，所以你只需给出你自己认为最接近的工作与差别，不必求全。

data.advice:
我会先核对工作区中的原始证据和前两项项目记录，再查最接近的交易成本与组合构建工作。本轮会重点检验：哪些是已知约束在该账户上的量化结果，哪些足以构成新的研究贡献，以及低价差情景会推翻哪些结论。目前可用的是题面摘录；本轮无法直接打开工作区、重跑测试或联网核验，因此我会明确区分摘录支持的结论与尚未核实的叙述。已经能确认一个关键问题：7.6bp 包含未测量的 5bp 滑点；另外，年换手 ≤6 并不推出每月、每个 sleeve 都有相同的硬预算。这两点会直接影响“三态接口是必然结论”的论证。贡献的边界更清楚了：固定费用形成不交易区域、整手约束形成离散持仓，已有直接前人工作；它们不能单独证明“三态”是必要接口。更可能成立的贡献，是测出资本、费用与执行规则何时让不同模型产生相同的可执行路径。但现有“清关率低于 50% 就不可测”的规则，还没有建立这种辨识能力；A 股个股符号预测如何转成债券、黄金和海外 sleeve 的收益与风险预测，也仍缺具体定义。**值得继续一次范围明确的验证；目前最有希望的贡献是“执行约束下的可辨识性与实证边界”，而不是“三态配置”或“估计广度与持有广度解耦”本身。** 冻结表、可行性报告和测试降低了实现风险，但还没有证明这项研究贡献成立。

以下依据题面摘录作判断，未独立读取原文件、重跑测试或联网核验文献。文件引文按所附行号定位；P1/P2 的原始记录缺失会单独标明。

1. **Q1：问题值得解决，但需要收窄问题的表述。**

   对 5万—10万元、按月决策的个人账户，预测产生的目标调整可能被最低佣金、整手和执行费用吞掉。这会让上游模型的改善无法成为可观察的账户收益。报告中，15.1bp 容忍度下，2.5% NAV 的调整在三个资本规模上均为 0% 清关；12.5% 的调整则大部分可以清关。这足以支持研究“小账户上的预测改善何时能转化为执行差异”。出处：`evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:31`、`evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:34`。

   但“账户买不起广度”说得过头。宽基 ETF 已经提供底层分散性；受到限制的是**独立调整风险暴露的粒度和成本效率**。持有 ETF 数量少，也不妨碍研究者观察大量未持有资产，因此持仓数量不能直接决定预测研究的统计功效。

   当前可用答案是静态配置、低频再平衡、现金吸收小额差异。其实际年度成本尚未给出。作为数量级，若一年只有四笔非零订单，最低佣金合计为 20 元，价差等费用另计；主动方案必须证明增加的决策值得付出额外费用与工程时间。现有可行性表说明了某些动作难执行，尚未说明这个简单答案哪里不够好。

2. **Q2：cannot judge — because 没有 P1/P2 的原始文件、代码位置或可定位账本记录，无法满足“每项历史主张给出 file:line”的要求。**

   题面将 P1 描述为：优化某种 reward，reward 与净收益的 Spearman 为 −0.043，账户从 100,000 降至 5,946.37。这只能作为待核叙述。若记录准确，它首先提示目标函数与最终效用脱节；缺少奖励定义、持仓约束、成本分解及归因，不能把亏损直接归因于成本，也不能据此判断模型类别失败。

   题面将 P2 描述为：存在正 rank IC，但毛收益不足以覆盖换手费用，唯一净正收益臂几乎不交易。若记录准确，它支持“排名预测有效不等于可交易收益有效”；还需要同暴露、同持有期的比较，才能区分成本节省和风险暴露变化。上述数字的出处目前只有题面 `problem` 段，**没有可核对的文件行号，我不给它们补造引用**。

   当前设计中可以定位的改变是：网络比较移到 panel 层，订单在取整后接受成本门控。这是合理的修正，但不能倒推为前两个项目失败原因已被完整查明。出处：`docs/direction-architecture.md:31`、`docs/direction-architecture.md:161`。

3. **Q3：最接近的前人工作首先是固定交易成本下的组合优化。**

   - **Lobo、Fazel、Boyd（2007），《Portfolio optimization with linear and fixed transaction costs》**，*Annals of Operations Research* 152，341–365 页；[作者页面与论文入口](https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/portfolio.html)。它已经处理线性费用与固定费用共同作用下的组合优化，明确了固定费用带来的非凸交易选择。费用导致不交易、交易选择需要显式建模，这些已有直接前例。
   - **MOSEK《Portfolio Optimization Cookbook》第 6 章、§6.2 “Fixed transaction costs”**，[具体章节](https://docs.mosek.com/portfolio-cookbook/transaction.html#fixed-transaction-costs)。这里给出了用交易指示变量建模固定买卖费用的实现方式。它说明此类约束可以进入标准优化系统，无须先发明三态接口。
   - **Gu、Kelly、Xiu（2020），《Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning》**，*Review of Financial Studies* 33(5)，2223–2273 页，[论文定位](https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhaa009)。它已经在大规模股票面板上比较线性与非线性预测，并通过投资组合评价经济价值。“大面板估计，再经组合构建检验经济收益”本身已有成熟路径。

   本方向的实质差别可以是：中国个人 ETF 账户的最低佣金、整手、结算与小资本约束，如何改变模型差异的可执行性和可检验性。上述工作没有替你完成这项具体测量，也没有替你解决 A 股预测向债券、黄金及海外 ETF 的迁移。但这些差别目前仍是**待完成的问题**，不能仅凭列出约束就算作贡献。

4. **Q4：贡献可以落在应用实证与度量上；目前不足以认定 framing 构成新方法。**

   我最不接受的推导是：存在最小清关金额，因此配置层必须使用三个状态。固定费用可以产生不交易区域，整手产生离散持仓；这两者都没有推出每个 sleeve 恰好需要 `{0, 1/2, 1}`。连续目标加不交易带、累积调整、达到门槛后一次交易，同样可以满足执行约束。三态是一个需要比较验证的设计选择。架构中“must therefore emit”超出了现有证据。出处：`docs/direction-architecture.md:192`。

   可行性论证还加入了一个额外政策限制：**年换手 ≤6 并不推出每月最多 50%，更不推出每个 sleeve 每月最多 12.5%。** 它至多给出平均额度；可以在月份之间、sleeve 之间集中使用。因此，“10bp 在 50k/75k 下超预算”是均匀分配政策下的结论，不能写成资金规模决定的不可行性。出处：`evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:19`。

   更有价值的贡献应当回答：给定资本、费用、整手和交易政策，**上游预测需要改善多少，才能改变可执行路径并产生可检测的净收益？** 要使它成为研究贡献，需要：

   - 将清关率连接到模型间的执行差异、独立决策日期数和最小可检测收益，而非任意采用 50% 阈值。
   - 在相同信号下比较连续目标加带宽与三态政策，在相同执行器下比较 ridge 与 MLP，并纳入已承诺的静态基线。
   - 展示边界随资本、实测执行损耗及费用方案的变化，说明结论适用于什么范围。

   如果最后只有费用公式、取整和审计账本，它仍然可以是有用的开放工程成果。“将 feasibility 作为一等产出”是一种良好研究实践；要进一步成为方法贡献，需要新的辨识指标、推导或有外部解释力的实证规律。

5. **Q5：1–2bp 会推翻具体门槛数值，但不会自动消除小额调整的成本问题。**

   在其余费用不变、且将 \(s\) 视为与原假设同口径的单边执行损耗时：

   \[
   c(N)=\max(5/N,\;0.00025)+0.00001+s.
   \]

   由此可得下表。最小金额尚未考虑各 ETF 的整手取整。

   | 单边执行损耗 \(s\) | 费率下确界 | 10bp 容忍度下最小金额 | 15.1bp 容忍度下最小金额 |
   |---|---:|---:|---:|
   | 5bp | 7.6bp | 约 10,204 元 | 5,000 元 |
   | 2bp | 4.6bp | 约 6,329 元 | 约 3,846 元 |
   | 1bp | 3.6bp | 约 5,618 元 | 约 3,571 元 |

   在 75,000 元账户上，15.1bp 对应的最小调整约从 6.67% 降至 4.76%–5.13%。但 2.5% 调整只有 1,875 元，光最低佣金就达到 26.67bp，因此仍不能通过这个容忍度。低价差会移动边界；它既不能证明三态必要，也不能证明连续微调已经经济可行。原文明确承认 5bp 未经测量：`docs/direction-architecture.md:275`。

   我会采用两个明确的停止结果：

   **结束“三态为必要接口”的主张：**在实测费用下，连续目标加不交易带满足相同换手与风险约束，并稳定取得更好的净结果，或者三态没有可重复的执行、收益或复杂度优势。

   **结束当前主动预测方向：**在独立保留样本中，所有预先声明的主动臂相对静态基线的年净增益，其置信区间上界仍低于经济门槛，例如 75,000 元账户的 375 元/年。这里需要证明有足够辨识能力；仅仅“区间包含零”可能是不确定，不能同时宣称策略无效和实验不可测。

   还应撤回“清关不足 50% 就不可测”的现成结论。少量交易可能足以检验低频策略，全部清关也可能让两个模型产生完全相同的订单。清关比例不能替代辨识能力。现行规则甚至把 executable months 与 folds 作比例比较，口径需要修正。出处：`docs/direction-architecture.md:219`。

6. **Q6：账户系统可以交付；完整预测研究的可交付性尚不能确认，瓶颈首先是目标定义和数据。**

   冻结输入、费用重算、取整、门控与确定性重放，都属于现有技术可以实现的工作。12M×60 的 float32 特征矩阵本体约为 2.9GB，工作站可以处理这一数量级；但这不能证明 MLP 每折一小时内完成，也不能证明全部研究只需 5–7 天。需要一个完整 refit 的时间和内存基准。

   当前最严重的接口缺口在 L1：E1 写的是个股未来 21 日收益符号，再按 sleeve membership 聚合；这没有定义债券、黄金和海外袖套的预测来源，也没有给出从符号概率到 \(\mu,\sigma,ES\) 的校准方法。出处：`docs/direction-architecture.md:207`。12M 行可以帮助估计个股关系，但不会增加共同月度择时目标的独立历史次数。可以明确固定其他袖套，只检验股票仓位择时；那时应同步收窄研究主张。

   成本数据也需要补齐：普通日线 OHLCV 不能直接测出下单时的买卖价差、深度或实际执行损耗。原文提出“from ETF bars”测量这些量，若只有日线，数据不足。出处：`docs/direction-architecture.md:275`。报价价差与原先的单边滑点还必须统一口径。

   **真正迫使设计的单一要求，是模型增量必须经过完整执行约束后仍可在样本外辨认，并达到经济门槛。**它要求共同执行器和状态账本；它没有要求三态或神经网络。另一个边界必须保留：若 27% 是绝不可突破的硬回撤保证，月度 95% VaR 加事后淘汰无法提供该保证，架构中的构造仍只能作为风险预算。出处：`docs/direction-architecture.md:55`。

data.advice:
1. **Q1: Is the problem worth solving? What breaks today, for whom, and what does the current answer cost?**
   Yes, the problem is valid and worth solving for a 50,000–100,000 CNY retail A-share ETF account rebalancing monthly under an annual turnover cap $\le 6$. What breaks today is the standard continuous-weight portfolio pipeline: at this capital scale, two structural frictions—the 5 CNY minimum commission floor and 100-unit board lots—interact with high-par ETFs and turnover caps to create a bimodal feasibility regime (0% vs. 93.9%–100% cleared cells in `evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:23-39`). Specifically, under the 5 CNY commission floor, 0.1 bp transfer fee, and 5 bp assumed slippage, the one-way cost rate has a hard infimum of 7.60 bp (`docs/direction-architecture.md:180`), and clearing a 15.1 bp gate requires a minimum post-rounding notional of 5,000 CNY (10.0% / 6.67% / 5.0% of a 50k / 75k / 100k NAV, `evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:12`). Meanwhile, four nominal stabiliser/bond ETFs (`511010`, `511260`, `511880`, `511990`) trade at ~100–141 CNY per share, making a single 100-unit lot cost 9,999–14,135 CNY (20.00%–28.27% of a 50k account, `evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:48-53`), rendering continuous tilts or small rebalancing trades impossible. Ignoring this and optimizing proxy rewards or unconstrained turnover breaks the account in net CNY, as shown by the prior projects losing ~94% of capital in P1 or netting $-5.73$ bp/trade in P2.

2. **Q2: What did each earlier project actually try, and what did its failures teach? Cite the file and line for each claim.**
   - **Prior Project 1 (P1) and Prior Project 2 (P2):** As summarized in the direction statement (`record:53`), P1 optimized a proxy reward that had a Spearman correlation of $-0.043$ with net return and ran 100,000 CNY down to 5,946.37 CNY; P2 achieved a genuine rank IC of 0.0707, but its 1.102 turnover paid 11.02 bp in transaction costs against 5.30 bp gross return, netting $-5.73$ bp, while its only net-positive arm barely traded. Both projects measured transaction costs ex post, and neither gated orders on post-rounding costs before execution.
   - **Earlier iterations of the current project (v1–v3):** Attempted to fit a neural network directly on the ~900 basket-month allocation sample while claiming trivial CPU scale (`docs/direction-architecture.md:54`), and relied on a realised-drawdown check to enforce a 27% drawdown ceiling (`docs/direction-architecture.md:55`). Those failures taught two lessons recorded in `docs/direction-architecture.md:54-60`: (i) a 50-observations-per-parameter budget caps a 900-row fit at ~18 parameters (`docs/direction-architecture.md:36-38`, `record:41`), so high-capacity learning must move to the 12M-row stock panel (`ashare_v2.duckdb`, `docs/direction-architecture.md:20-21`) and compress through a $\le 4$-parameter combiner (`docs/direction-architecture.md:54`); and (ii) continuous sleeve tilts at 50k–100k get suppressed into `FIXED` by the 5 CNY fee floor (`docs/direction-architecture.md:60`), forcing the L2 interface in v11 (`record:53`) to emit discrete sleeve states ($\{0, 1/2, 1\}$ of budget, `docs/direction-architecture.md:189-192`).

3. **Q3: What is the closest prior work — a paper, a repository, a product, or code in this workspace? Name it with a location and say what it already settles.**
   - **In academic literature:** Boyd, Busseti, Diamond, Kahn, Koh, Nystrup, and Speth (2017), *"Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization"*, Foundations and Trends in Optimization, Vol. 3, No. 1, pp. 1–76 (specifically Section 3 on transaction cost envelopes and Section 7 on non-convex minimum-trade thresholds and lot rounding; open-source reference implementation in `cvxportfolio`), alongside Garleanu and Pedersen (2013), *"Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs"*, Journal of Finance 68(6):2309–2340. These works already settle that proportional plus fixed/minimum transaction costs create a no-trade region and that small accounts under minimum fee floors must trade in discrete lumps rather than continuous increments.
   - **In this workspace / ecosystem:** Microsoft's `Qlib` (`qlib.contrib.strategy.signal_strategy` / `TopkDropoutStrategy` and `qlib.backtest.exchange`) and the local panel store referenced at `D:/minequant/AlphaGPT/data/ashare_v2.duckdb` (`docs/direction-architecture.md:21`). Qlib already settles the panel-level workflow of comparing linear models against MLPs on A-share daily panels and routing top-K signals into a discrete-lot backtester.
   - **Substantive difference:** Prior work treats lot rounding and minimum-commission suppression as an execution post-processor on top of continuous target weights, and evaluates panel models primarily on cross-sectional IC or large-capital portfolios where $N \gg N_{\min}$. This project's distinct angle is proving—and enforcing as a hard software contract (`record:53`, `docs/direction-architecture.md:158-169`)—that at 50k–100k CNY, the post-rounding fee gate (`N_min`) exceeds the continuous weight increment (`docs/direction-architecture.md:187-192`), which collapses the admissible L2 action space to $3^4 = 81$ discrete states and requires decoupling estimation breadth ($N \approx 5,820$ stocks) from holding breadth (4 investable ETF sleeves + cash) behind a $\le 4$-parameter bottleneck.

4. **Q4: Where could a new contribution land, and what would have to be true for it to count as one?**
   The primary contribution lands on **systems engineering and empirical measurement (making capital-scale feasibility a first-class, falsifiable research artifact and establishing "unmeasurable at this capital" as a rigorous scientific conclusion)**, and only secondarily on the **estimation-vs-holding breadth decoupling framing** if E1 succeeds.
   - Because fixed-cost no-trade zones and two-stage panel-to-index aggregation are theoretically known, the conceptual framing alone is not a standalone theoretical breakthrough.
   - However, elevating the feasibility map (`evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:1-64`) and the 8-invariant append-only ledger (`docs/direction-architecture.md:156-169`) into a hard gate that prevents unexecutable signals from masquerading as alpha *is* a genuine methodological and systems contribution for small-account quantitative research.
   - For the **decoupled estimation-to-discrete-combiner framing** to count as an empirical modeling contribution as well, two things must hold in E1 (`docs/direction-architecture.md:196-217`): (1) the sleeve-deviation share of score variance must be $\ge 20\%$ (`docs/direction-architecture.md:59`), proving the 12M-row panel provides cross-sleeve differentiation rather than a disguised 1-factor market-timing bet; and (2) the panel-fed discrete combiner must beat the static annual-rebalance baseline net of costs while keeping executable months $\ge 50\%$ (`docs/direction-architecture.md:216-217`).

5. **Q5: Which observation would end this direction? Name a result that would make you abandon it.**
   - **Observation that kills the prediction/active-allocation branch:** In E1 (`docs/direction-architecture.md:208-217`), either (a) executable months fall below 50% of folds (`docs/direction-architecture.md:216-217`), (b) the sleeve-deviation share of score variance is $< 20\%$ (`docs/direction-architecture.md:59`) *and* neither Ridge nor MLP beats the static annual rebalance net of cost (`docs/direction-architecture.md:266-267`), or (c) on the cheapest separator, the sleeve-level rank correlation with next-month sleeve returns is indistinguishable from zero for both Ridge and MLP.
   - **What happens if measured one-way spread is 1–2 bp instead of the assumed 5 bp (`docs/direction-architecture.md:273-275`):** If realised one-way slippage is 1 bp (instead of 5 bp), `var = transfer + stamp + slippage` drops from $5.1\text{ bp}$ to $1.1\text{ bp}$, and the one-way rate infimum `commission_rate + var` drops from $7.60\text{ bp}$ to $3.60\text{ bp}$ (`docs/direction-architecture.md:178-181`). Does the discretization conclusion fail? **No, at tightly controlled tolerances (e.g., $T = 7.6\text{ bp}$ or $10\text{ bp}$), it remains binding, whereas at $T = 15.1\text{ bp}$ it relaxes only partially:**
     - Using the exact formula `N_min = max(5 / (T - var), ceiling)` (`docs/direction-architecture.md:181`), the 5 CNY commission floor still binds up to `N = 5 / 0.00025 = 20,000 CNY`.
     - At $T = 7.6\text{ bp}$ with $1.1\text{ bp}$ var, $N_{\min} = 5 / (0.00076 - 0.00011) = 7,692.31\text{ CNY}$ (15.4% of a 50k NAV, still outside the 12.5%/sleeve turnover budget).
     - At $T = 10\text{ bp}$ with $1.1\text{ bp}$ var, $N_{\min} = 5 / (0.0010 - 0.00011) = 5,617.98\text{ CNY}$ (11.2% of 50k, 7.5% of 75k — still a coarse ~8–11% lump, essentially equivalent to the current 15.1 bp regime).
     - At $T = 15.1\text{ bp}$ with $1.1\text{ bp}$ var, $N_{\min} = 5 / (0.00151 - 0.00011) = 3,571.43\text{ CNY}$ (4.76% of 75k NAV), which would allow 5-state $\{0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1\}$ steps instead of 3-state $\{0, 1/2, 1\}$ steps, while board-lot granularity on high-par ETFs (`511010`, `511260`, `511880`, `511990` at 10k–14.1k CNY/lot, `evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:48-53`) remains completely unchanged because lot size depends on price, not spread.
     - Even if spread dropped to 1 bp *and* tolerance remained at 15.1 bp, what remains of the direction is still its core structural thesis: **sample-size decoupling** (10 ETFs have a rank IC standard error of 0.333 vs. 0.032 on the 1,000+ stock panel, and ~120 months still cap the allocation combiner at $\le 4$ parameters) and **post-rounding ledger gating**.

6. **Q6: Could a system deliver this with the data, compute, and time this project actually has? Name the single requirement that would force the design, or say that no available system could.**
   *(Emphasis: system — hardest scrutiny applied here.)*
   Yes, the system can be delivered on the single Windows workstation (with local DuckDB `ashare_v2.duckdb` at 12,008,787 rows and RTX 5060 / CPU) within the 5–7 engineer-day budget, **provided** three concrete system-architecture seams that currently threaten the invariants and E1 validity are closed.
   - **The single requirement that forces the design:** The combination of `scale` and `interface`—fitting on 12M daily stock-panel rows across 13 annual folds while constraining the allocation interface (`L2`) to $\le 4$ fitted parameters over a discrete $3^4 = 81$-state space and gating every post-rounding order at `N_min = max(5 / (T - var), ceiling)` inside a deterministic, hash-chained append-only ledger (`docs/direction-architecture.md:158-192`).
   - **System vulnerabilities where this design is fragile:**
     1. **State-dependence breaks pure one-way L1 $\to$ L2 $\to$ L3 decoupling:** Under a post-rounding order gate (`docs/direction-architecture.md:161-162`), whether a transition from current holdings $w_{t-1}$ to a discrete target state $s_t \in \{0, 1/2, 1\}^4$ clears `N_min` (e.g., 5,000 CNY) depends on the *trade delta* $|w_{t,\text{target}} - w_{t-1,\text{actual}}| \times \text{NAV}_t$, not on the target state $s_t$ alone. In `docs/direction-architecture.md:282-286` and `docs/direction-architecture.md:201-202`, how the $\le 4$-parameter combiner is fitted over the ~120 months is underspecified: if L2 fits its 4 parameters against frictionless sleeve returns without simulating the stateful L3 gate, it can learn transitions (e.g., $0 \to 1/2$ at 50k NAV when sleeve budget is 12.5k, or drift-induced partial steps) that L3 deterministically suppresses; conversely, if L2 optimizes net CNY through the non-differentiable L3 gate over 81 states, it requires a discrete grid/coordinate search coupled to the ledger replay.
     2. **Cross-class settlement and order-sequencing deadlock in L3:** Invariant 4 (`docs/direction-architecture.md:163-164`) states that *"A sell's proceeds are unavailable to buys until settlement of its instrument class; a T+1 buy cannot be sold same session"*, while Open Item 5 (`docs/direction-architecture.md:287-288`) admits that T+0 vs. T+1 by class is still a design assumption, not a measured fact. In a monthly rebalance where cash is only the residual (`interface`), rotating from an equity ETF (e.g., `510300`) into an overseas/commodity ETF on the same monthly decision timestamp requires cash before the buy can execute. If the sell proceeds settle T+1 (or even if cash is unavailable intra-bar until fill ordering is defined), a single-timestamp monthly rebalance batch will either reject the buy for insufficient settled cash or require a two-phase execution state machine (sell on day $t$, buy on day $t+1$) that exposes the book to overnight gap risk and alters `NAV` hash replay.
     3. **Point-in-time stock-to-sleeve aggregation leakage at L1:** E1 predicts stock-level 21-day forward return signs on `ashare_v2.duckdb` (5,820 codes) and aggregates them *"by sleeve membership to a sleeve score"* (`docs/direction-architecture.md:204-206`), while L1 exports *"per-sleeve mu, sigma and expected shortfall per month"* (`interface`). First, rank predictions (return signs) do not natively have the units of `mu`, `sigma`, and `expected shortfall`—the calibration mapping from cross-sectional stock rank/sign to sleeve-level $(\mu, \sigma, \text{ES})$ is a hidden model layer that could smuggle in extra parameters or break the $\le 4$-parameter budget if fitted. data.statement: At retail capital the admissible order — not the portfolio weight — is the unit of decision: measure how many (month × instrument) cells clear a fixed 5 CNY / 100-share-lot gate, report the smallest executable action, and let that measurement decide the action set.
data.problem: Three review rounds left the direction blocked on five high objections because it asked a 900-row basket-month sample to carry a model that needs millions of rows, and because a realised-drawdown check cannot enforce a prospective ceiling. The prior two projects fix the constraint: P1 optimised a reward with Spearman -0.043 against net return and ran 100,000 to 5,946.37; P2 had real rank IC 0.0707 but turnover 1.102 paid 11.02 bp against 5.30 bp gross, netting -5.73 bp, and its only net-positive arm barely traded. Both measured cost and neither gated on it. At the same time the account cannot buy breadth: a rank IC standard error is 0.333 at ten names versus 0.032 at a thousand, so any ETF-level cross-section at 50k is unmeasurable. The resolution is to estimate where the sample is large, hold where the account is large enough to hold, and make the interface between them small enough to be tested.
data.difference: Against v3 this replaces three things rather than rewording them: (1) training moves to the panel layer and the 'scale: trivial CPU on 900 rows' claim is withdrawn, with refit CPU-minutes measured instead; (2) the 27% ceiling becomes a construction (1-month 95% VaR <= d_max/6) plus a drawdown throttle plus an evaluation rejection rule, instead of a realised-drawdown check; (3) uncertainty is a 6-month moving-block bootstrap over calendar dates that preserves cross-sleeve correlation, and the sleeve score is decomposed into a common monthly factor plus deviations, so a single market-timing bet is named as such when the deviation share is below 20%. Against the two prior projects the difference is that the model's output is a cost-gated order inside an account ledger, and adoption requires beating a same-feature ridge on net CNY rather than on IC or reward.
data.learn: E1 tells whether nonlinearity adds monthly cost-clearable information at this panel size: ridge versus MLP, identical features and folds, both routed through the same account engine, adoption only if the MLP wins >=70% of folds, has a 90% block-bootstrap CI of net difference excluding zero, and adds >=375 CNY/yr at 75,000 CNY. A null says nonlinearity is not where the money is at this sample and closes the prediction branch; it says nothing about learned predictors as a class.
data.minimalTest: Cheapest separator: fit ridge and a small MLP on the same frozen panel features for one fold, aggregate both to inclusive sleeve scores, and compare the sleeve-score rank correlation with realised next-month sleeve returns while reporting the sleeve-deviation share of score variance. If the MLP's score is indistinguishable from ridge's at the sleeve level, no account-level replay can rescue it and E1 can be shortened to the score comparison.

data.subject: the five separable contributions C1-C5 against the prior-art check of 2026-11-04
data.decision: Prior art disposed of: C1 adapt (Baule 2010 owns the fee-floor mechanism and the wealth→n* map; only the empty feasible set is ours and it belongs to C4), C2 adapt (BSCV 2009 owns the few-parameter policy; our two-layer split is defended only by parameter count and declared a trade-off), C3 adapt with a change of baseline ({0, full} is the fixed-cost default, the half state is a treatment), C4 adapt and concentrate the contribution there (cleared-cell share and smallest executable action have no published analogue), C5 vocabulary only (Crosby-Wallach tamper-evident wording; dropped from the contribution list). Rejected: DVC (dvc/repo/index.py:123 silently drops an algorithm-mismatched hash — the exact failure newquant/ledger.py:96 exists to prevent), the three-state grid as a deduction, and Garleanu-Pedersen as support (their post-eq.10 aside describes the quadratic-cost branch we are not in).
data.rationale: Each verdict came from reading the source rather than the abstract, and each disposition changes a concrete artifact: the doc's §1 claims, §6 scope, §5 invariants, and the action-set comparison in build step 6. Nothing was adopted that does not change a decision or a number.
data.applicability: Holds for a CN A-share ETF account of 50k-100k CNY trading monthly at a 10-30 bp tolerance, with a 5 CNY commission floor and 100-share lots; the 5 CNY floor is regulatory (免5 prohibition) and a change to it voids the granularity numbers.
data.remainingRisk: The novelty claim now rests on a single metric measured on one venue and one capital range; if the metric is judged obvious the contribution collapses to engineering. Baule's n*≈2-3 at this capital also predicts the four-sleeve book is over-broad at 50k, which the granularity table supports (10.0% of NAV per action at 15.1bp).
data.verifyPlan: Read MMOR 2012 (DOI 10.1007/s00186-012-0408-3) in full; if it formalises the empty feasible set, downgrade C4 to 核心已有 and move the contribution to the account-level net-CNY engine instead.
data.reopenCondition: A paper that already reports an admissibility metric for retail orders, or a rule change to the 5 CNY floor, or a full-text read of MMOR (2012) showing it formalises the empty-feasible-set case.

findings.text: 当前可见的 E1 定义没有给出个股符号预测向债券、商品、海外袖套的映射，以及向收益、波动和短缺风险的校准；补齐前，完整 L1—L2 比较实验尚未定义完成。
findings.author: gpt-6.1-sol
findings.quote: "Monthly forward sleeve return rank, computed from the sleeve's index series; the panel model predicts stock-level forward 21-day return signs, aggregated by sleeve membership to a sleeve score."
findings.response: Conceded. The three-state grid no longer follows from the cost formula. §5 now says the action set is compared: {0, full} is the baseline because fixed-cost theory gives a single non-zero action (Altarovici-Muhle-Karbe-Soner arXiv:1306.2802 §1: rebalancing is a bulk trade to the frictionless target), and the half state is the treatment. Build step 6 replays both through the same executor. The continuous-weight alternative is also still admissible as the third arm.

findings.text: The fee calculation establishes a minimum admissible order; it does not establish that the resulting band compensates for exposure drift. The proposed experiment must demonstrate that additional economic claim.
findings.author: gpt-6.1-sol
findings.quote: "Commission is 5 CNY floored per non-zero order, so a 5,000 CNY order pays 10.0bp of commission alone; adding 5bp slippage and 0.1bp transfer gives 15.1bp one-way at that boundary."
findings.response: Conceded, and the arithmetic is now explicit rather than a policy. Turnover 6 is a pool: 300,000 CNY/yr at 50k. At a 15.1 bp tolerance the smallest executable action is 5,010 CNY, so the pool funds 52 lumps and the budget never binds at any NAV in range. The 12.5%/sleeve uniform split is withdrawn. What the gate destroys is resolution, not measurability: N_min/NAV is 10.0% at 50k, 6.7% at 75k, 5.0% at 100k (evidence/feasibility-d6a6e438.md:62-82).

findings.text: Under the stated maximum of twelve instruments and quarterly net rebalancing, eliminating commission-floor surcharges alone cannot clear the 375 CNY annual hurdle: its ceiling is 240 CNY, excluding common entry and exit. A passing result needs cost and exposure attribution.
findings.author: gpt-6.1-sol
findings.quote: "The predeclared hurdle for the whole experiment is 0.5 percent of capital per year, about 375 CNY on 75,000."
findings.response: Half-conceded, and the honest half is a bound rather than a number. Daily bars cannot price the spread here: Corwin-Schultz produces 47.2% negative two-day pairs and Roll is identified on only 4 of the 11 tradable codes (estimators_failed=true). What the data does support is the exchange tick: half a tick is 0.04-4.90 bp by price, and the all-in floor is 3.4-7.5 bp on the tradable set, with 512100 at 7.50 bp — essentially the inherited infimum. Market impact remains unmeasured and is now labelled as the single remaining assumption rather than a measured input.

findings.text: The population measurement establishes granularity by instrument classification. It does not measure the claimed relationship between granularity and portfolio stability. That claim requires risk evidence for the actual holdings and target portfolio.
findings.author: gpt-6.1-sol
findings.quote: "Within fixed income, granularity and stability are therefore anti-correlated at this capital, and the only finely divisible stabiliser is uninvested cash, which carries no lot constraint at all."
findings.response: Conceded. E1 is scoped to the equity sleeve only. The mapping is explicit: stock-level predictions are aggregated with point-in-time index weights from index_weight_pit (000300.SH, 000905.SH, 000852.SH, monthly with available_date) plus a reported coverage share, so a prediction over 40% of the basket cannot be reported as covering the sleeve. Calibration is separated from prediction: mu is the score scaled by realised cross-sectional dispersion over the same membership, sigma and ES come from the sleeve's own trailing 24-month returns. The model never supplies a distribution.

findings.text: The cost gate requires a minimum post-rounding executed notional of ~5,000 CNY to cap the 5 CNY commission floor at 10.0bp (15.1bp total one-way), which means in a 50,000 CNY account across 8-12 ETFs (average sleeve 4,166-6,250 CNY), every partial drift rebalance trade is smaller than 5,000 CNY and will be permanently suppressed by the post-rounding gate, turning the band rule into a no-trade freeze except on full sleeve liquidations.

findings.quote: "Commission is 5 CNY floored per non-zero order, so a 5,000 CNY order pays 10.0bp of commission alone; adding 5bp slippage and 0.1bp transfer gives 15.1bp one-way at that boundary."

Measurability is now a power statement published before the verdict: with about 120 monthly decisions and measured dispersion s of the monthly net-CNY difference, the 80%-power MDE is about 2.8s/sqrt(120); if that exceeds the 375 CNY/yr hurdle the verdict is 'unmeasurable at this capital' with the number attached, and no claim is made in either direction.

findings.response: Conceded. Invariant 9 is added: a rotation that must both sell and buy is two-phase — sells settle on their class date (T+1 equity and overseas, T+0 bond and commodity) and buys are placed only against settled cash. findings.text: If the learned model is fitted on aggregated features at the basket-month level (~900 observations), the hard gate of 50 observations per parameter caps the model at ~18 parameters, which deterministically triggers the failure-handling fallback for any neural network; for a neural network to ever execute without violating the gate, estimation must occur on the stock-level cross-sectional panel before basket aggregation, which contradicts the `scale` assumption that model training is trivial single-process CPU compute on 900 rows.

The seq-68 response fields on F-fe8c8bdf-4, F-60b5f78a-1/-2/-3/-5 and F-113a8e8d-1/-2/-3/-4 are therefore not evidence of an answer to those objections. 3) Id-keyed disposition of the nine direction objections: F-fe8c8bdf-1 (three-state grid not deduced) answered by comparing the action set, {0,full} baseline vs half treatment, docs/direction-architecture.md:236-248; F-fe8c8bdf-2 (turnover pool, not per-month per-sleeve cap) answered at :249-256, 300,000 CNY/yr funds 52 lumps so the constraint is resolution not spend; F-fe8c8bdf-3 (7.6 bp is conditional, not measured) answered at :258-270 with the tick-floor bound, half a tick 3.4-7.5 bp, Corwin-Schultz and Roll failures reported in evidence/spread.json; F-fe8c8bdf-4 and F-fe8c8bdf-6 (no stock-to-sleeve mapping or calibration for bond/commodity/overseas) answered by narrowing E1 to the equity sleeve at :261-269 plus the separated calibration at :279-283; F-fe8c8bdf-5 (the 50%-of-months rule has no power basis) withdrawn, replaced by the published MDE 2.8 s/sqrt(120) at :294-300; F-fe8c8bdf-7 (combiner's discrete rule and objective) narrowed at :236-248 and :270-274 to four fitted parameters on (score, vol, ES, deviation) fitted pre-gate, with the grid as one arm; F-fe8c8bdf-8 (the floor rests on unmeasured 5 bp) accepted, the 1 bp half-spread is unreachable against a 3.4 bp tick floor so it stays only as a sensitivity row; F-fe8c8bdf-9 (I-4 settlement blocks a monthly sleeve rotation) answered by invariant 9, two-phase execution, at :200-205. F-113a8e8d-5 (a basket-month-level fit cannot carry a network under 50-observations-per-parameter) is answered in kind by design v12 placing estimation at the stock panel over 12.0 M rows, and stays open only as an unmeasured budget until E1 records refit CPU-minutes per fold. 4) Verified input facts on the local panel D:/minequant/AlphaGPT/data/ashare_v2.duckdb (read-only, queried this session): index_weight_pit holds exactly three indices — 000300.SH 77,050 rows over 257 monthly dates 2005-04-29..2026-08-31, 000905.SH 129,540 over 260, 000852.SH 142,300 over 143 from 2014-10-31 — weights summing 99.5-99.9 per date, and available_date lagging trade_date by a median of 3 days (max 12), so every fold must join on available_date, not trade_date; there is no PIT weight for 399006.SZ, which confirms the equity-sleeve scope 510300/510500/512100 rather than an omission. daily_bar has 12,008,787 rows over 5,820 codes 2014-01-02..2026-10-15 with adj_factor never null, and daily_price_limit (12.3 M), daily_suspension (321,929 S / 14,446 R, with available_at) and daily_basic_pit (12.0 M rows of pe_ttm, pb, turnover_rate, total_mv, circ_mv) supply the tradability filters and the feature base. 5) Adopted: seq 68 is not review evidence; the disposition above stands as the objection record; build step 5 (E1) starts on this panel with ridge and the small MLP on identical features, annual refit, 2016-2025, and the three-part adoption rule unchanged; a future cross round answers by objection id, using the patched responses schema (presets/personal-quant/kernel.js:4004 schema, :4481 id-first matching, :4616 and :4645 unmatched reporting).

Every one of the nine direction objections has an artefact behind it that can be read without a reviewer, and the three that seq 68 flagged as unanswered are answered in the document; what the round actually exposed is a kernel defect that misfiled answers, which is fixed rather than argued with. Recording the disposition also fixes the ledger's own accuracy: three objections currently read open that are answered, and nine older ones carry response text that belongs elsewhere. Proceeding to E1 is licensed by the same reading the document already makes — the remaining doubts (slippage, settlement table, CPU budget) are measured inside E1 or labelled as assumptions, not prerequisites for starting it.

If a PIT weight source for 399006.SZ or a constituent bridge for the bond, gold or overseas sleeves appears, the sleeve count in scope changes and objections F-fe8c8bdf-4/-6 reopen at the wider scope, not at this one.
data.remainingRisk: Reviewer availability is the live risk: gemini4high failed 2 of 6 rounds and gpt-6.1-sol aborted on the one cross round it was given, so a future round may again return nothing; a round with no reviewer text must be recorded as void rather than as a verdict. Substantively, the 5 bp slippage and market impact stay unmeasured (labelled, not solved), the T+0/T+1 table stays an assumption until invariant 9 is exercised, and F-113a8e8d-5's parameter-count objection is only answered once E1 records actual refit CPU-minutes per fold.
data.verifyPlan: Run E1's first fold end to end: build features from daily_bar + daily_basic_pit with the limit and suspension filters, join index_weight_pit on available_date, fit ridge and a small MLP on identical features, and report the coverage share plus the sleeve-level rank correlation against realised next-month sleeve returns. If the pipeline leaks, the tell is a fold whose out-of-sample IC collapses when available_date is lagged one extra month; if the panel cannot populate the sleeve at all, coverage share comes back near zero and the scope claim is wrong.
data.reopenCondition: Reopen if any of the following appears: a reviewer returns usable text that contradicts one of the dispositions above; E1 finds coverage share below about 40 % of the traded basket weights, which would invalidate the sleeve aggregation rather than the model; or a fourth index with PIT weights is added to the panel, changing E1's scope.

data.subject: E1 build: reuse what the local panel already implements; reject qlib/rqalpha as dependencies; write the model layer and the sleeve aggregation
data.decision: E1's L1 layer is built in newquant from the local contracts, not on top of qlib or rqalpha. Dispositions: (a) REJECT qlib as a dependency — it is the only open stack that covers rolling-training plus ridge/MLP (RollingGen at qlib/workflow/task/gen.py:142, LinearModel RIDGE at qlib/contrib/model/linear.py:30, DNNModelPytorch at qlib/contrib/model/pytorch_nn.py:39, RollingEnsemble at qlib/model/ens/ensemble.py:65, SigAnaRecord/PortAnaRecord at qlib/workflow/record_temp.py:302/365), but its feature universe is price/volume only (Alpha158 = $close72/$volume33/$low16/$high15/$open13/$vwap2, no size or valuation), its processor layer has no tradability or suspension handling (grep for tradable|suspend over qlib/data/dataset/processor.py returns nothing), it has no index-weight concept (scripts/data_collector/cn_index/collector.py:162 keeps only 证券代码 and drops the weight column; grep for $weight across the repo returns nothing), and trade_unit=100 is inert whenever trade_w_adj_price=True (qlib/backtest/exchange.py:750/775/783). Wiring it to ashare_v2.duckdb would mean writing a handler that replaces the expression layer anyway; the two things worth having (rolling fold generation and per-fold model fit) are ~200 lines against contracts we already own. (b) REJECT rqalpha as an engine (event-driven, commercial licence for production) but ADOPT one semantic: its PIT stamp-duty switch (rqalpha_mod_sys_transaction_cost/deciders.py, STOCK_PIT_TAX_CHANGE_DATE=datetime(2023,8,28), tax_rate=0.001 before and 0.0005 after). Applied here this closes the F-60b5f78a-4/6 contradiction in the only way that matters for us: the traded instruments are ETFs, which are stamp-duty exempt, so any borrowed cost model must set stamp_tax=0 rather than inherit a 0.0005 constant — the local AlphaGPT default at ashare_data/config.py:494 would otherwise charge 5 bp on every sell that does not exist, which is larger than the 3.4-7.5 bp all-in floor this project measured and would corrupt the band gate. (c) ADOPT the local AlphaGPT data contracts as specification, not as import: T+1 entry (ashare_portfolio/rebalance.py:88 entry_offset=1), adjusted-price basis with no ffill (ashare_data/processor.py:421), fail-closed tradability (ashare_model/data_loader.py:926), and the OOS stitch contract (ashare_model/eval_metrics.py:579). Reimplemented in newquant/panel/{source,features,model,aggregate}.py because importing that engine also imports ashare_model/factors.py:227 fillna(0.0), which makes a missing feature indistinguishable from a cross-sectional median and lets a model learn from a stock's absence — a hard defect for supervised learning, and one the 74-name frozen grammar at ashare_model/vocab.py:221 would freeze into E1 too. (d) REJECT vectorbt (Apache-2.0 plus Commons Clause, LICENSE.md withholds the right to sell) and backtrader (GPL-3.0, copyleft). (e) ACCEPT that PIT index weights have no open implementation (akshare's closeweight file carries a single date, 20261030; tushare pro.index_weight needs 2000+ credits; baostock ships membership lists only) and that the point exists locally in index_weight_pit — so the as-of reader is 40 lines (newquant/panel/source.py) and the sleeve aggregation that consumes it (newquant/panel/aggregate.py) is the part of E1 with no prior implementation anywhere, local or open source. Honest consequence recorded: E1's novelty is the aggregation and the coverage term, not the predictor.
data.rationale: The question was whether E1 needs to be written from scratch. The panel is local (ashare_v2.duckdb, 28 tables, verified by tests/test_panel_contract.py), so no open project supplies it; the computation shell is already implemented locally but its missing-feature convention and frozen grammar make it a bad host for a supervised target; the only open stack with the model layer (qlib) would have to be re-plumbed to a panel it cannot express. What must be written is therefore narrow and explicit: a per-fold fit-predict loop, an as-of weight reader, and the stock-to-sleeve aggregation with a coverage term. That is what build step 5 now is.
data.remainingRisk: Reimplementing the data contracts means the local engine's own leakage guards (its 5 PIT mechanisms) are not inherited; the only guards now are newquant's own tests, which cover the feature-vs-future half but not the membership half, and the weight staleness (one month by construction) is a real limitation of every sleeve score E1 produces.
data.verifyPlan: Run E1 end to end; if the ridge arm's out-of-sample IC is implausible (far above the single-feature ICs it is built from) then the contract reimplementation leaked, and the leakage test in tests/test_panel_features.py is the first thing to distrust and extend.
data.reopenCondition: If a maintained open implementation of point-in-time index weights with historical weight columns appears (or tushare access is obtained with 2000+ credits), the as-of reader should be replaced by it rather than maintained here. If qlib's handler layer gains a PIT weight field and a tradability processor, the dependency question should be re-asked.

data.subject: E1 build scope, with its applicability
data.decision: E1 is built in newquant on the local panel; only the per-fold fit loop, the as-of weight reader and the sleeve aggregation with a coverage term are new code
data.rationale: The earlier record of the same conclusion carried no applicability, so the state view filed it under hypotheses and a reader could not tell when it stops being true. This restates it as a scoped claim and points at the evidence rather than repeating it.
data.applicability: Holds while (i) the only price/fundamental source is the local ashare_v2.duckdb panel with its index_weight_pit table, (ii) the traded instruments are A-share ETFs (stamp-duty exempt) whose sleeve members are the three bridged indices, and (iii) the model layer under test is ridge or a small MLP, for which qlib's expression/handler machinery would have to be replaced rather than reused. It does not claim qlib is unsuitable for price/volume-only Chinese equity research, nor that a borrowed cost model is wrong for stocks.
data.remainingRisk: By reimplementing the local contracts instead of importing them, E1 does not inherit that engine's membership-integrity guards; the only guards now are newquant's own tests, which cover the feature-vs-future half and not the membership half.
data.verifyPlan: If the ridge arm's out-of-sample IC lands far above the single-feature ICs it is built from, the contract reimplementation leaked and the leakage test in tests/test_panel_features.py is the first thing to distrust.
data.reopenCondition: A maintained open implementation of PIT index weights with historical weight columns, or qlib gaining a PIT weight field plus a tradability processor, reopens the dependency question; a change of traded instrument away from ETFs reopens the stamp-duty conclusion.

data.subject: E1 out-of-sample IC and the ridge-vs-MLP gap
data.decision: E1 first full run: mean monthly rank IC is 0.065 (ridge) and 0.070 (MLP) out of sample on the 3 634-name index-member population, 2016-2025. The MLP's mean \u0394IC is +0.0051 with a 6-month moving-block bootstrap 90% CI of [-0.0045, +0.0137], so nonlinearity is NOT certified at the pre-registered bar even though it wins 8 of 10 folds; clause (iii), the net-CNY term, is still open until build step 6. Sleeve deviation share is 0.40 (ridge) / 0.32 (MLP) of score variance, so the three bridgeable sleeves are not one factor. Mean coverage runs 0.93 (2016) to 0.998 (2020 onward), so the coverage term is near-inert after 2019. 2017 inverts for both arms (IC -0.053 / -0.037), which is the case for a gate that suppresses trading on a weak score. Refit cost is 2.96 CPU-minutes for ten folds, which closes the refit-budget objection.
data.rationale: This is the first measured outcome of the branch the whole direction depends on, and it is a null on the registered nonlinearity clause rather than a win, so it has to be recorded before step 6 is built on top of it: if the MLP is not certified, step 6's policy comparison should carry the ridge arm as the predictor of record instead of averaging two unvalidated arms.
data.applicability: Holds for this panel (14 features, 21-session forward return, annual refit, monthly signal dates, 3 634 index-member names, 2016-2025 out-of-sample). Says nothing about other feature sets, other horizons, shorter refit intervals, or the full market population; a longer sample or a different target horizon could move both the level and the ridge-vs-MLP gap.
data.reopenCondition: A feature set with cross-sectional valuation and liquidity controls available in 2016-2019 changes the comparison; if MLP's fold advantage concentrates in the years where ridge lambda hit 0.3, then lambda selection is the active ingredient rather than the nonlinearity, and the arm should be re-specified before the direction is read as a null on learned predictors.

data.decisionRule: PRIMARY cell = NAV 75,000, tolerance 15.1 bp, measured per-instrument slip (0.0005/median close). Adopt the state-conditioned arm over static-annual iff BOTH (i) the 6-month moving-block bootstrap (2000 draws, seed 20261104) 90% percentile CI of the annualised net-CNY difference d_t = (r_arm_t - r_static_t)*NAV0 excludes zero, AND (ii) the point estimate is >= 375 CNY/yr (0.5% of capital). If the CI contains zero the reading is "no measurable net value at this capital and cost" and the pre-reserved reading band-rule-demoted-scoped applies - not a reason to retune the gate. Independently, if MDE = 2.8*sd(d_t)/sqrt(120) > 375 the verdict is "unmeasurable at this capital" with the number attached. The tolerance sweep {10, 15.1, 30, 50, 75} bp and NAV {50k, 100k} are descriptive evidence for the same question, not separate adopt/reject tests; if they disagree in sign with the primary, the primary is reported as tolerance-dependent and nothing is adopted. A baseline that is frozen by the gate at the primary tolerance is itself a result (it answers F-113a8e8d-6) and does not license changing the tolerance to make the baseline trade.

data.subject: trade policy for the ETF-only mandate at 50-100k: which of static-annual / vol-conditioned / four-parameter band rule to run
data.decision: No trade-policy change is adopted, and the question is closed at this capital. The unconditional static-annual mandate at the frozen venue is the operating policy; `vol-conditioned` and `rule` are not adopted at any NAV level. Three consequences are adopted with it: (1) the equal-weight-within-sleeve allocation rule is withdrawn and must be replaced by one in which each member's own sleeve slice clears that member's own post-rounding cost floor, or the sleeve drops to fewer members (design v13 candidate, not recorded as a design version until it can be reviewed); (2) any future arm comparison must run at a gate where the baseline trades, and must report the baseline's terminal wealth across the tolerance sweep as its control; (3) the next build step for this line is forward paper trading of the frozen venue plus the static mandate, not another arm on the same 2016-2025 window.
data.rationale: The pre-registered rule fired three independent failure conditions at once: the 90% interval covers zero, the minimum detectable effect (1,750 CNY/yr) is 4.7x the 375 threshold that would have to be cleared, and the sign of the difference reverses both across the tolerance sweep and across NAV. Separately, the measurement established that the cost gate - not the arm - decides what the account holds: 90.2% of intents sit below the clearing floor, the overseas sleeve is never entered, and loosening the gate alone moves the baseline from 94,978.68 to 133,645.14 with no strategy change. Retuning the gate in response would be fitting the result. What would change this: a venue where the per-order minimum is smaller relative to NAV, a NAV where the sleeve slices clear (approximately above 120k on this venue), or an arm whose trades are not functions of the same volatility estimate that the baseline already responds to.
data.applicability: A-share ETF-only account, 50,000-100,000 CNY NAV, the 11-code frozen venue (venue_hash d6a6e438e32e818f), per-order commission floor 5 CNY with 2.5 bp above it, monthly decision calendar with annual arm refit, 2016-2025 data. Does not apply where the commission floor is absent or proportionally smaller, above roughly 120,000 CNY where the overseas sleeve clears, to intraday or multi-asset mandates, or to instruments outside the frozen venue. The dividend/unito-change accounting and the I-1..I-9 invariants hold independently of this decision and are unaffected by it.
minority: The vol arm's point estimate is above the threshold (+417 vs 375) and it is the only arm whose point estimate clears the bar; a reading that treats a positive point estimate with a CI covering zero as pure noise discards the directional information the design is built to exploit, and the worse drawdown is the cost of the same mechanism rather than evidence against it.
data.remainingRisk: The comparison is against a baseline the gate froze, so "not adopted" is a statement about this gate at this capital, not a refutation of volatility conditioning in general: at 30 bp the vol arm loses 177 CNY/yr while at 10 bp it gains 915, and neither is certifiable. Only one 10-year window and one venue were read. The overseas sleeve's unenterability is a consequence of the 5 CNY floor being regulatory; if that floor moves, the constraint that produced this reading disappears with it. The static mandate itself remains a bet on five premia, not a measured edge.
data.verifyPlan: Cheapest check that would show this wrong: run the 30 bp cell (where the static arm trades 32 times) with one arm that is not a function of the same 60-session volatility estimate, and see whether its delta is positive with a CI excluding zero on the same 120 monthly decisions. A second, cheaper check: compute the same deltas at 120,000 NAV, where the overseas sleeve clears, and see whether the ranking changes.
data.reopenCondition: A change in the per-order commission floor; a NAV at or above roughly 120,000 where every sleeve slice clears its member floors; or a gate tolerance at which the baseline itself trades combined with a candidate arm not derived from the baseline's own state variable.

The cost gate is not a friction on drift but a constraint on the initial allocation. At 75,000 and 15.1 bp the clearing floor per code runs 3,345.02 (511220) to 5,066.23 (512100); 90.2% of all sized intents fall below it; the overseas sleeve's per-code slice is 2,500 against its worst member's 4,436, so 33 intents over ten years fill zero times.

Because the overseas sleeve is never entered, the arm called static-annual is not a policy: it holds 33.19% of NAV in cash at entry, 10.46% at the end, and its realised equity weight is 0.3806 against a 0.45 target.

Loosening the gate alone, with no change of strategy, moves the baseline's terminal wealth from 94,978.68 to 133,645.14 CNY (+40.7%) across the {10, 15.1, 30, 50, 75} bp sweep. Any arm comparison at a gate that freezes the baseline measures the gate.
The difference's sign reverses on both axes of the sweep: vol signs +,+,-,-,- and rule -,+,-,-,- across tolerance; rule is +259 at 75,000 but -18 at 50,000 and -5 at 100,000.

Dividends are measured, not assumed: 9,390.40 CNY credited as cash on ex-dates from the fund's own distribution record, 30.5% of the static arm's 30,810 total gain, about 1.25 pp of annual return and 2.5x the comparison margin. eastmoney qian fuquan was rejected as a source: A = qfq/raw drifts nonlinearly for 9 of 15 codes, so inverting it books drift as distributions.

Slippage is a measured floor (half tick per instrument), not an impact model: the flat-5bp and worst-half-tick rows at the primary cell give delta_vol +930 and +88, so the ranking is not stable in the cost model either.
