data.statement: At 50,000-100,000 CNY the binding constraint on a durable A-share return is executable structure, and E2 located it precisely at the initial allocation rather than at rebalancing: with a 5-CNY per-order commission floor and the measured half-tick spread, the minimum clearing order is 3,345-5,066 CNY, so a sleeve's per-member slice - not its drift - decides whether the sleeve exists. The contribution is therefore a floor-aware sleeve composition, in which the member count per sleeve is chosen so every member's slice clears its own minimum order, held statically and audited in an append-only net-CNY ledger, with the shipped claim gated by a forward paper book. Trade policy is closed as unmeasurable at this capital: the band rule and volatility conditioning both failed the pre-registered net-CNY test.
data.problem: Two prior projects on this machine built competent measurement machinery and both failed to produce net account returns, and the failure is arithmetic rather than subtle. P1 (D:/minequant/AlphaGPT) recorded negative_no_admissible_formula with 0 admissible arms, 6 of 55 candidates with positive excess and median excess -12.94%, while its selection objective had Spearman -0.043 against realised net return and its simulated account ran 100,000 to 5,946.37 (-94.05%). P2 (D:/进益资本杯) achieved real gross predictive content - rank IC 0.0707, residual IC 0.034, fusion dRankIC +0.01158 across 8/8 windows - and its own gate file prices the result exactly: gross long-short spread 5.30 bp per snapshot against turnover 1.102, so breakeven one-way cost is 2.40 bp, and at the project's own 5 bp stress rate the reference blend is net -5.73 bp per snapshot. In that same table the arm with rank IC 0.0070 and turnover 0.003 is the ONLY net-positive member (+0.17 bp), with breakeven 29.94 bp - a tenfold difference in the selection metric pointing the wrong way. Neither project put the account itself - CNY, the per-order fee floor, 100-share lots, settlement, cash - inside the loop being optimised. This line has now run that test to its end: E2 replayed three arms over 120 monthly decisions at 50k/75k/100k and found no certifiable arm difference (vol +417 CNY/yr, 90% CI [-716, +1666], MDE 1,750 against a 375 threshold), while the same replay showed the per-order floor silently deleting an entire sleeve and holding a third of the account in cash at entry. So the problem is no longer "which trade policy"; it is "which composition of instruments is expressible at this capital, and what does it return net of the structure that expresses it".
data.difference: Differs from both prior lines in the objective, not the model: they optimised a scalar reward and rank IC (reward-vs-net Spearman -0.043; rank IC 0.088 with net -0.9 to -4.2 bp/day), this line optimises net CNY of one small account. Within this line it differs from idea v5 in what the constraint is taken to bind: v5 located it in the trade policy (a band rule sized off the fee floor) and spent the budget proving that empty - E2 certifies nothing for either conditioned arm and closes that branch. What survives is the part v5 treated as a design assumption rather than a question: equal weighting inside a sleeve, with the per-member slice as the unit the floor acts on. That assumption is now known to be the binding one (90.2% of intents below the floor; overseas never entered in ten years) and it is cheap to test properly, because a floor-aware composition needs only 4-6 instruments at 50k rather than the 10-15 the frozen venue carries.
data.learn: Whether a floor-aware composition is expressible at 50,000 CNY and what it costs to hold. The arithmetic says it should be: at 50k with one code per sleeve, equity 22,500 against a 3,649 floor, bond 17,500 against 3,435, commodity 5,000 against 3,669, overseas 5,000 against 4,027, so four to six instruments clear every floor where fifteen did not. What would change my mind: a replay of the floor-aware composition at 50k/75k/100k showing (a) every sleeve entered, (b) realised weights within one board lot of target in most months, and yet (c) net CNY indistinguishable from the degenerate cash-heavy baseline the current design produced - which would say the constraining problem was never the floor but the instrument set, and the answer is to leave this venue rather than re-weight inside it.
data.minimalTest: Cheapest kill: a composition table plus one replay, no new data. For each NAV in {50k, 75k, 100k} and each sleeve, take the cheapest listed member by measured clearing floor and compute slice_cny = w x NAV / k against min_notional(15.1 bp, measured half tick) for k = 1, 2, 3; pick the smallest k that clears, and check the resulting instrument count is <= 6. Then replay that composition on the existing engine (newquant/replay.py already produces every input; the change is a member-selection function, not new machinery) for the same 2016-2025 window and report fills, realised-vs-target weight, net CNY and the ledger hash. Pre-declared reading: composition is adopted only if every sleeve is entered at all three NAVs and the account's realised equity weight is within 2 percentage points of target in at least 80% of months; otherwise the venue, not the weight vector, is the problem and the next question is instrument-set selection.

replaceable.claim: The allocation rule and the universe are swappable; the ledger, the cost accounting and the corporate-action application are not

cost.claim: The annual trading budget is 353 CNY at 75,000 (0.47% of capital) and the engineering is measured rather than estimated: step 6 cost 17 cells and 16.4 CPU-minutes

validate.claim: The shipped design is validated by a forward paper book - monthly decisions appended to the same ledger, marked to last close - not by the 2016-2025 replay, which can only screen

validate.measure: forward months recorded with realised net CNY, realised fill count per sleeve, and realised-vs-target weight; a sleeve never entered in the paper book is a design failure, not a market event

interface.claim: One CLI: composition table -> per-NAV replay -> ledger hash -> comparison against the cash-heavy baseline, emitting one JSON summary and one monthly parquet
interface.condition: the engine newquant/replay.py already accepts the NAV, tolerance and cost mode as arguments; only the member-selection function is new

dataFlow.claim: Composition first, orders second: sleeve weights and member counts resolve to instruments and slices, the floor check runs on slices, then the monthly loop reads ledger state, marks, rounds to lots, gates, executes sells then buys from settled cash, and appends
dataFlow.condition: the floor check must precede order sizing, because a slice that cannot clear cannot be repaired by a better gate at order time
dataFlow.measure: any sleeve that fails the slice check appears in the summary with the numbers that failed it, and the replay never emits an order for it

storage.claim: Append-only jsonl ledger per (arm, NAV, tolerance), parquet bars and corporate actions, a frozen venue parquet with content hash, and a monthly summary parquet
storage.condition: the ledger is the only source for state reconstruction and the only evidence a fill happened

data.subject: is a 35% bond sleeve implementable at 50k-100k on the frozen venue
data.decision: Measured: the bond sleeve is board-lot bound, not cost-floor bound. One lot of a par-quoted bond ETF is 10,000-14,135 CNY, about three times min_notional(15.1 bp) = 3,345-5,066. Realised bond weight at entry is 20.0% against 35% at 50k (-15.0 pp), 26.7% at 75k (-8.3), 30.0% at 100k (-5.0) in 2016, unchanged in 2020; equity is within -1.5 pp and commodity/overseas within -0.5. At 50k only 83.3% of capital is deployed, leaving 16.7% cash against a 10% target. So E2's static arm at 50k was in practice a 44/20/10/10 portfolio with 16.7% idle cash: its 3.19% CAGR describes the executed mandate, not the declared one.
data.rationale: A 42-second table settled what two design versions assumed: the cost floor was measured per code, the board lot never was.
data.applicability: Frozen venue, 35% bond sleeve, 50k-100k CNY, 2016-2022 while 511220 traded near par. After its 2023-01-16 10:1 split (lot 988) the gap is -1.4/-0.7/-0.4 pp. Sleeves priced under ~35 CNY express within 1.5 pp at every NAV.

data.subject: which entry condition and capital floor the next design version must carry
data.decision: Adopted from bond-sleeve-lot-bound (seq 85). (1) Design v14's entry condition is slice >= max(min_notional(tolerance, side), one board lot at that era's price); a slice can clear the cost gate and still be unbuyable, which is exactly what v13 missed. (2) The mandate stops being a weight vector below ~120,000 CNY: either the bond sleeve is defined in lots and its target weight becomes endogenous, or the capital floor rises to 120,000, where the lot rounds to within 2 pp. No third option on this venue - 511010/511260/511880/511990 are worse at 14,135/13,578/10,093/9,999 per lot. (3) My idea v6 acceptance criterion measured equity weight within 2 pp, which passes at -1.5 pp while bonds sit 15 pp off: the measure must be the worst sleeve, and that pre-registration is recorded as mis-specified rather than quietly amended.
data.rationale: The probe cost 0.7 CPU-minutes and pre-empted a replay that would have measured a portfolio 15 pp short of its own mandate. Arithmetic over frozen prices cannot be overturned by a better backtest, only by a cheaper bond lot.
data.applicability: Design v14 for the 50k-100k band on this venue. The 120,000 threshold follows from floor(0.35 x NAV / 10,000) x 10,000 within 2 pp of target and is venue-specific, not general.
data.remainingRisk: The return effect of the 15 pp bond deficit is unmeasured; it probably flattered the equity-led 2016-2022 result, sign and size unknown.
data.verifyPlan: Recompute the table per candidate venue, then one replay of a lot-defined mandate at 50,000 to price the deficit in CNY.
data.reopenCondition: A bond ETF with a lot under ~3,400 CNY enters the venue, or the bond weight is redefined in lots.

data.decisionRule: PRIMARY cell = NAV 50,000, tolerance 15.1 bp, measured per-instrument slip (0.0005/median close), window 2016-01-04..2025-12-31, cost model / calendar / execution path unchanged from E2. P1 CONTROL: arm `mandate` must reproduce E2's nav50000_tol15.1_measured static cell (nav_end 62163.64, n_fills 6, ledger head db6a4f19b62d1e759bd1c6177dee140f6c5cc46c5e6357053ed78b35cf07f1e9); if it does not, outcome = invalid_experiment and no reading is taken. P2 EXPRESSIBILITY (counting fact, not a return claim): per arm report cash weight at first and last decision, realised-vs-target per sleeve, codes never filled, and fills/intents. R1 passes for an arm iff every sleeve holds >= 1 member at the first decision and cash weight at the first decision <= 20%. P3 RETURN: annualised net-CNY difference d_t = (r_arm_t - r_ref_t) * NAV0 over 120 monthly returns, 6-month moving-block bootstrap, 2000 draws, seed 20261104, 90% percentile CI; MDE = 2.8*sd(d_t)/sqrt(120). Pairs: lots-mandate, lots_deploy-mandate, lots_deploy-lots, lots-cash, lots_deploy-cash. Drawdown and vol are reported with the same window, never as an adoption test. P4 FORM DECISION for design v14: among lot-defined arms, adopt the one whose 90% CI lower bound on d_t vs `mandate` is > 0. If no arm clears that bound, adopt the lot-defined form on P2 (R1) with the unexpressed fraction held as CASH - an unmeasurable return cannot license a risk-increasing redeployment tilt - and state the return effect as unmeasured with its MDE attached. A point estimate inside the MDE is reported as 'no measurable net value at this capital', never as a win. P5 CAPITAL OPTION: the nav120000_tol15.1_measured static cell is descriptive evidence for the alternative (raise the floor to 120,000 so lot rounding lands within 2 pp of target); it is not an adoption test, and the report must state the required capital in CNY rather than round the choice to a preference. P6 NO RETUNING: tolerance stays 15.1 bp, slippage stays measured, window stays 2016-2025, no arm may be resized to make it trade. An arm that cannot trade is a result (E2 already answered that question the same way).
data.notes: Arms are engine-level, not weights: `lots` and `lots_deploy` fix the COMPOSITION RULE and let the same plan_order gate and board-lot rounding decide every fill. Frozen rule details: (i) per sleeve k = largest member count in 1..len(members) such that declared_slice/k >= max over the kept members of max(min_notional(15.1, side), 100*mark); (ii) within the kept k, members are equal-weighted in SLEEVE_MEMBERS order, first k (frozen venue table order, not a ranking); (iii) expressed sleeve weight = sum(100*mark*floor(per_member/(100*mark)))/NAV, i.e. rounded DOWN to whole lots, cash is binding as in round_to_lots; (iv) `lots_deploy` redistributes the total unexpressed fraction pro rata to the declared weights of the sleeves that expressed within 1% of target, ONE pass, no iteration, then the engine re-rounds. `cash` arm = 100% cash, never trades, terminal 50,000 by construction; it is the 'do nothing' denominator, not a portfolio. This run answers seq 87 items 1-2; it does not start step 7 and does not touch the trade policy closed at seq 78.

data.subject: how the lot-bound residual is redeployed in the lots_deploy arm
data.decision: Amended the redeploy rule registered in run-e3c00001 (seq 88) before reading any full-window number. As registered: the residual goes pro rata over the sleeves whose expressed weight is within 1 % of their target. As amended: a sleeve is lot-bound iff its gap (declared - expressed) is positive and at least half of the total gap; the residual then goes to the remaining sleeves pro rata to their DECLARED weights, scaled to fill 1 - (sum of the bound sleeves' expressed weights) so the vector sums to 1.
data.rationale: The 1 % tolerance is not a rule at this capital, it is a coin flip: on 2016-01-04 commodity expressed 0.0990 against a 0.0990 threshold and overseas 0.0988, so commodity alone qualified and the rule lifted a 10 % sleeve to 23.8 % of NAV on a 0.0002 difference. A criterion whose outcome flips on the 4th decimal of a lot count cannot be pre-registered as a treatment, and the half-of-total-gap test identifies the same economic fact structurally: the shortfall belongs to the sleeve whose instrument quotes near par, because one board lot is 20 %+ of that sleeve's own target, not rounding noise. Also fixed: the first implementation scaled the free sleeves by (declared + total residual) / declared, which double-counted the free sleeves' own rounding gaps and pushed the target vector to 1.017 of NAV; the fill is now anchored to the bound sleeves' expressed weights, so the vector sums to exactly 1.
data.applicability: The lots_deploy arm of e3-composition-at-50k only. The lots arm (residual to cash) is unchanged, and no tolerance, slippage, window or size assumption moved.
data.notes: Disclosure: the 2016-only smoke replay (2016-01-04..2016-12-31, 50,000, tol 15.1) had already printed nav_end for the 1 % version before the amendment. That is one year of a 10-year window and it was read to debug the rule, not to choose it; the full window had not been run. The amended rule is strictly less arbitrary - it has no free parameter - and both versions remain reproducible from the recorded code hashes.

data.subject: how many instruments a 50,000 CNY account can express on the frozen venue at 2016-01-04: five, not six
data.decision: The expressible tree at 2016-01-04 with NAV 50,000 is 5 instruments - equity 2 (510300, 510500), bond 1 (511220), commodity 1 (518880), overseas 1 (513100) - not the 6 recorded by the composition probe. The probe's equity k = 3 counted 512100, which does not list until 2016-11-04: probe_table.py skipped a member with no price via `if px is None: continue` instead of dropping it from the sleeve's member list, so an unlisted fund inflated the count by one. The bond conclusion the probe was run for is unaffected (bond k agrees at 1), as are commodity and overseas (both agree at 1). The engine's newquant.replay.lot_composition is now the single owner of this rule; the probe's table is reconciled against it (evidence/e3-report.md section 7) rather than trusted on its own.
data.rationale: One rule with two owners is a defect, and the reconciliation found a real disagreement rather than assuming agreement: 2016-01-04 probe total 6 vs engine 5, with equity 3 vs 2 and the cause named (unlisted_at_ref 512100). The engine never admitted an unlisted member, so no E2 or E3 replay number changes; only the probe's instrument count and the derived statement that the 50k tree holds 6 codes. The 75k/100k maxima in the same table inherit the same flaw wherever 512100 or any other unlisted member was counted, and must be recomputed by the engine before reuse.

data.subject: which composition form design v14 carries, and what E3 measured for it at 50,000 CNY
data.decision: Design v14 carries the LOT-DEFINED mandate with the residual held in cash, and it supersedes the weight-vector mandate of design v13. Concretely: each sleeve declares a member list; the member count k is the largest value for which each member's slice clears max(that code's 15.1 bp gate, one board lot at that era's price); the sleeve's realised target weight becomes what its whole lots are worth, rounded down; whatever the mandate cannot express in whole lots stays in cash and is priced, not redeployed. `lots_deploy` - the variant that pushes the residual into the sleeves that did express their target - is NOT adopted even though its point estimate is higher, because its gain over the cash-residual form is unmeasurable (lots_deploy - lots = +387 CNY/yr, 90% interval [-71.6, 973.7], MDE 933). The capital-floor option of seq 86 (raise the mandate to 120,000) is recorded as available and NOT adopted: at 120,000 the bond sleeve quantises to 0.6 pp at the last decision and 0.6 pp at entry (34.44 % held against a 35 % mandate), which is better than the 2 pp seq 86 predicted, but it buys about a point of sleeve fidelity for 2.4x the capital, while the lot form delivers the measured composition gain at the capital the mandate names. Sleeve fidelity must from now on be read from `aimed` (the decision target after whole lots) and never from `realised` (the same sleeve a month later, which also contains its own price drift) - seq 86's 15 pp bond deficit was an `aimed`-class statement and stays valid at entry, while the 7 pp `realised` gap at the last 120k decision is drift, not quantisation.
data.rationale: E3 priced three things design v13 did not have. (1) The E2 execution left 37.4 % of the account in cash at entry (0.40899665 at the first month end), held commodity and overseas at 0 % for all 120 months, and traded 3 codes; the lot-defined form enters with 19.6 % cash, holds 1 commodity and 1 overseas member on day one, and trades 5 codes. (2) That composition difference is worth +1,542.8 CNY/yr net of costs against the E2-executed arm, 90 % interval [857.8, 2212.6], MDE 1393 - it separates from zero, and the control arm reproduces E2 exactly (62163.64 / 6 fills / head db6a4f19), so the difference is composition and not a drifted execution path. (3) The idle cash is the object v13 was missing: 11252 CNY first-order for the static arm (254.2 bp of NAV0 per year) versus 6297 for the lot form and 3010 for the redeploy variant. The redeploy variant's extra 387 CNY/yr is 4.0x its own MDE away from resolution, so choosing it would be trading an unmeasured gain for a higher risk load: it raises entry equity from 39.7 % to 52.0 % and entry commodity/overseas from 10.2/9.9 % to 12.7/12.6 %. The pre-registered conservative branch (lot form, residual to cash) is the answer, and the tie-break is stated here rather than discovered afterwards. Separately, the 120k comparison confirms the venue arithmetic but not the reason seq 86 gave: bond lots cost ~10000 CNY at par in 2016 and 511220 trades at 100.00 on 2016-01-04, so the 2016 quantisation at 120k is 0.56 pp; by 2025 511220 is at 10.2 post-split and 511380 at 13.7, so the same capital no longer buys the same fidelity. A capital floor is therefore not a permanent fix on this venue - it is a fix that decays as the bond funds' prices move.
data.applicability: A-share ETF-only accounts, 50,000-100,000 CNY, on the frozen 11-code venue (venue_hash d6a6e438), tolerance 15.1 bp, measured per-instrument slippage, 2016-01-04 .. 2025-12-31. The k rule is venue arithmetic, not a market claim, and travels with the venue.

data.subject: which parts of composition-entry-condition-v14 (seq 86) the adopted v14 decision keeps and which it replaces
data.decision: composition-mandate-v14-lot-defined (seq 93) supersedes seq 86 only in part, and the supersedes link over-reaches as written. KEPT from seq 86: point (1), the entry condition slice >= max(min_notional(tolerance, side), one board lot at that era's price), and the observation that a slice can clear the gate and still be unbuyable. REPLACED: point (2), which offered two options - bond sleeve defined in lots, or a 120,000 capital floor - because E3 measured the first and priced the second, so the choice is no longer open; and point (3)'s pre-registration wording, which measured equity weight within 2 pp instead of the worst sleeve, which now reads as a historical note rather than a live rule. data.rationale: The supersedes edge is all-or-nothing in the record model, and marking an entire record superseded when its central clause is retained would mislead a later reader into rebuilding the entry condition. data.purpose: A fresh session is resuming the etf-implementable-frontier line and must not adopt the handoff's next step unread. Independent read before any new subsystem (the forward paper book) gets built.
data.question: Read the handoff as a record, not a plan. (a) Which of its claims are backed by an artefact I can re-read, and which are one session's reading? (b) Its 'next' step 1 is to build a forward paper book (a new subsystem) while step 2 is a cheap sleeve-decomposition replay of E3. Given that the only measured positive result is lot-form minus control = +1,542.8 CNY/yr with a 90% interval [857.8, 2,212.6] and MDE 1,393 — i.e. a margin of only ~1.1x over MDE, on a single 50,000 CNY cell, in-sample 2016-2025 — does building the paper book follow, or is the E3 result too thin and too single-cell to license five years of forward measurement? Which cheap measurement would you demand first, and what result would make the paper book pointless?

data.advice:
I’ll assess what the cited artifacts support, then examine whether the handoff’s ordering follows from those results. I’ll first check whether the underlying reports are accessible here.The E3 result is positive, but its comparison is narrower than the proposed forward test: it measures the lot-defined portfolio against an E2 control that permanently omitted commodity and overseas exposure. I don’t have filesystem access in this session, so I’m working from your supplied facts and excerpt; I can identify which artifacts would verify each claim, but cannot claim to have re-read them.**I would reverse steps 1 and 2 and defer building the forward paper book.** E3 supports a positive historical improvement over a constrained control at 50,000 CNY. It warrants a cheap investigation of where that improvement came from. It does not yet justify choosing a new subsystem and five years of forward observation as the next experiment.

My reason is broader than the roughly 1.1× effect/MDE ratio: E3 changes the portfolio’s attainable exposures, the proposed forward comparison changes the benchmark to cash, and neither robustness across capital nor the forward experiment’s power has been established.

**The strongest objection to that conclusion is that E3 is already a meaningful positive result.** Its reported 90% interval excludes zero, the control reproduces E2, and forward observation could address uncertainty that further historical analysis cannot resolve. A minimal monthly paper record could also be inexpensive. I accept that objection: this result deserves follow-up. But it favors proceeding promptly with the cheap diagnostic and then designing the forward measurement. It does not explain putting the diagnostic second.

The MDE ratio needs careful handling. MDE is a power calculation under specified assumptions; exceeding it by only 1.1× does not invalidate the reported interval. Conversely, exceeding it does not establish durability or justify a particular forward horizon.

I cannot access `D:/newquant` in this session. The distinction below is therefore between claims with named, rereadable supporting artifacts and interpretations in the supplied handoff—not a claim that I independently verified those files.

| Claim | Evidential status |
|---|---|
| E3 terminal values, fills, monthly outcomes, estimated differences, intervals and MDEs | These have named support in `e3-report.md`, `e3-summary.json`, `e3-monthly.parquet` and the ledgers. The report’s estimator and uncertainty method still need inspection. |
| E3 control reproduces E2 exactly | A concrete consistency claim that can be checked against both runs’ outputs and ledgers. Matching terminal value, fills and ledger head supports implementation consistency; it supplies no independent economic validation. |
| E1 does not certify the MLP’s improvement over ridge | Supported by the stated ΔIC interval and attributed to `e1-report.md`. This concerns the incremental benefit of nonlinearity. It does not settle the usefulness of the underlying signal or allocation. |
| The trade-policy line is closed | The arithmetic, 40 × 8.82 = 352.8 CNY below 375, follows directly. Its scope depends on the order-count and saving-per-order bounds applying to the policies under consideration. |
| v14 was adopted, earlier records were corrected, and review rounds are exhausted | These are provenance and workflow claims, checkable in the cited ledger records. Adoption establishes a decision; it does not establish empirical validity. |
| “The bond lot is the binding constraint,” the lot-defined mandate is the right next design, and a paper book will license the shipped claim | These are interpretations or decisions. The probe and E3 may support narrower versions, but the reported totals alone do not establish them. |
| Build steps are “done” | A completion assertion until checked against code, run manifests and acceptance criteria. An artifact can demonstrate that a run occurred without demonstrating that the research question is resolved. |

The distinction that matters most is between **“this different implementable allocation performed better in this period”** and **“we have identified a durable advantage worth measuring through this particular forward design.”** E3 directly supports the former. The handoff advances to the latter without completing the attribution work it already identifies.

The first measurement I would demand is **a paired sleeve-removal replay of E3, with an implementable static comparator**:

1. Freeze the existing window, capital, costs, gate and lot rules. Reproduce the reported `lots − control` estimate using the report’s exact estimator.
2. Remove each sleeve from **both** arms, routing its allocation to cash under a declared rule. Measure how the paired difference changes. Prioritize bonds, commodities and overseas exposure, because those are the competing explanations in the handoff.
3. Compare `lots` with a simple, lot-feasible static portfolio using the same available sleeve menu and cash convention. Establish what the proposed mandate adds beyond obtaining those exposures.
4. Report the contributions by fixed chronological blocks from the monthly series, then replay one adjacent capital cell. Those are robustness diagnostics, not fresh holdout evidence.

Removing a sleeve only from `lots` would answer how much that sleeve helped `lots`; it would not cleanly attribute the advantage over control. Also, removal effects need not add up: cash, lot feasibility and the gate can interact. Report those interactions instead of forcing an additive explanation.

This is a small extension of an existing replay whose six runs took 30.6 seconds. It should precede a subsystem build.

**What would make the proposed paper book pointless depends on the claim it is supposed to establish.**

- **If the advantage disappears against the feasible static comparator, and the attribution explains essentially all of E3’s uplift through exposures absent from E2,** a bespoke paper-book subsystem has little value as evidence for an additional decision rule. The remaining proposition is a simpler allocation proposition, which can be evaluated with a correspondingly simple record.
- **If the advantage depends on one historical episode, disappears at nearby capital, or collapses when a listing or execution assumption is corrected,** the current evidence would not support committing to the proposed forward experiment.
- **If five years cannot resolve the intended economic benefit against the intended benchmark,** that horizon is unsuitable as the promised certification route. Continuing to collect observations would not repair an inadequately powered design.

There is an important qualification to the first condition: finding that commodity or overseas exposure explains the gain would **not by itself discredit the allocation**. Enabling useful exposures may be exactly the benefit of a lot-defined mandate. It would narrow the claim and could substantially simplify what needs to be built.

Likewise, an ablation interval crossing zero would not establish futility. A stronger stopping result would put the **upper uncertainty bound below a predeclared minimum useful benefit**, or show that the proposed strategy is mechanically equivalent to the simpler comparator. The 375 CNY trade-policy hurdle should not automatically become the composition hurdle.

**What would change my conclusion:** a compact replay showing an economically useful advantage under accurate execution assumptions, explaining its sleeve sources, and showing that it survives reasonable chronological and capital checks. Broad contribution from every sleeve is unnecessary; a defensible source of return is enough. I would then support a minimal forward book with a frozen comparator, endpoint, useful-effect threshold and explicit power calculation.

That last calculation must use the proposed forward comparison. E3’s `lots − control` MDE does not power a future `lots − cash` test. For illustration only, under ordinary square-root-of-time scaling, reducing ten years to five would raise the **same-comparison** MDE from 1,393 to roughly 1,970 CNY/year—above the observed 1,543. The actual calculation depends on the estimator and return dependence. The supplied handoff does not establish that five years is enough.

Exhausting review rounds is a workflow constraint. It supplies no evidential reason to prefer building over measuring, and future paper returns cannot automatically resolve the open design findings.

**My confidence is high, about 85%, in putting the cheap measurement first.** My confidence that the allocation itself will fail is much lower. The supplied evidence supports further investigation; it leaves the source, robustness and appropriate forward test insufficiently resolved.

data.hypothesis: E3's +1,542.8 CNY/yr for the lot-defined arm over the static control is mostly the acquisition of the commodity and overseas sleeves, not the lot rule: on the frozen venue the static arm holds commodity 0.00% and overseas 0.00% for all 120 months while the lot arm holds ~9.5-11.6% and ~9.8-10.3%. Zeroing those two sleeves out of BOTH arms, with the removed weight left in cash and no renormalisation of the others, should collapse most of the paired difference.
data.decisionRule: Report lots-static for five declared mandate variants at 50,000 CNY (full, no_commodity, no_overseas, no_both, no_bond) with the same 6-month moving-block bootstrap as E3. Retain the composition claim only if the no_both delta stays at or above 60% of the full delta (~925 CNY/yr) with an interval excluding zero; narrow it to 'hold every sleeve with one lot' if it falls below 30% (~463) or its interval includes zero. Also report lots-static at 75,000 and 100,000, and the same-comparison MDE recomputed on 60-month subsamples, because the proposed forward book is a 5-year lots-vs-cash test and E3's MDE does not power it.
data.notes: explore step, not confirm: an attribution probe on existing replays, no new mandate. Disposable script; the point is whether the confounded exposure channel explains the E3 number.

data.subject: What E3's +1,542.8 CNY/yr actually measured
data.decision: E3's lot-defined mandate adds nothing on top of merely holding commodity and overseas: zeroing those two sleeves out of both arms (removed weight to cash, no renormalisation) drops lots-static to -19.6 CNY/yr [-99.4, +28.7] from +1,542.8 [857.8, 2212.6], a share of -1.3% against a pre-declared 30% narrowing threshold, and the collapse repeats at 75,000 (+1,910 -> -103.5) and 100,000 (+1,166.7 -> -47.9). The surviving claim is 'hold every sleeve with at least one lot, residual to cash'; the sleeve tree and its k-selection carry no measurable content once the exposures exist.
data.rationale: The control's executed path is measured: 37.39% cash at entry, commodity and overseas 0.00% for all 120 months (E2 62,163.64 / 2.20% CAGR / 6 fills, reproduced to the cent by E3's control check); the seq-85 sentence calling E2 'in practice 44/20/10/10 with 16.7% idle cash at 3.19%' describes the probe's hypothetical, not E2. Removing one sleeve at a time retains 48-62% of the pair (no_commodity +959.7, no_overseas +742.8), so single-sleeve ablations understate the confound: the sleeves are substitutes, not additive parts, and only joint removal closes it. Removing bond instead raises the pair to +1,773.4, locating the effect in equity/commodity/overseas occupancy rather than in the bond sleeve. What would change this: a control that holds one lot of every sleeve and still separates from the lot arm.
data.applicability: Frozen 11-code venue (venue_hash d6a6e438), 2016-01-04..2025-12-31, 15.1 bp per-order gate, measured slippage, equal weight within sleeve, residual to cash (no redeploy). Holds while the control's commodity and overseas slices stay below one board lot at the stamped NAV; at a capital where the declared 10%/10% slices already clear one lot the confound disappears by construction and both arms hold all four sleeves.
data.reopenCondition: A mandate that keeps all four sleeves in the control (one lot each) and still separates from the lot-defined arm, or an instrument whose lot is small enough that the static split buys commodity and overseas at 50,000.

data.subject: Can a forward paper book certify a claim at 50,000 CNY
data.decision: No forward comparison at 50,000 CNY is powered to certify either live claim, so handoff step 1 (a five-year paper book scored net CNY against a same-window cash arm) cannot license the shipped claim. Measured on the same monthly series: lots-cash is +2,851.2 CNY/yr with MDE 3,819.2 over ten years, and the 60-month MDE is 6,007 (first half) / 4,770 (second half) - above the effect at every horizon a paper book would realistically run. The composition contrast is worse: lots-static +1,542.8 with a 60-month MDE of 1,666.2-2,244.3. Reaching MDE = effect needs ~1.8x the ten-year sample for lots-cash (~18 years) and ~2.1x for lots-static (~10.6 years), at the measured 9.40%/8.63% vol and the same estimator.
data.rationale: MDE_Z 2.8, 6-month moving-block bootstrap, 2,000 draws, seed 20261104, and the ten-year variance as the variance estimate; the 60-month numbers are the same estimator on truncated delta series, not a sqrt-time approximation, and they agree with the sqrt-time scaling (~1.41x the ten-year MDE within each half's own variance). The advisor's pre-declared stop was 'the upper bound of the effect interval sits below a minimum useful benefit, or the design is mechanically equivalent to the simpler comparator'; the attribution record meets that stop on its own, and this power arithmetic means accumulating observations would not repair it. What would change this: a materially lower-variance mandate, or a paired shadow-arm difference series measured small enough that a five-year MDE falls under the effect.
data.applicability: 50,000 CNY, 9-9.4% annualised vol, monthly decisions, ten years of history as the variance estimate. A lower-volatility book or a paired design with a smaller difference-series variance lowers the MDE; a longer horizon lowers it only as sqrt(years).
data.reopenCondition: A forward instrument with materially lower return variance (bond-heavy or hedged book), or a paired shadow-arm design whose difference series is measured to have variance small enough that a five-year MDE falls below the effect it must detect.

data.subject: What the forward book measures after the attribution killed the return claim
data.decision: The line's forward step is an execution-conformance book, not a return paper book. What is measurable at 50,000 CNY within ~12 months is whether the mandate is executable: sleeve occupancy, cost in bp, and the reason for every suppressed intent. What is not measurable is any net-return claim. Acceptance at 12 month-ends, declared now: (a) commodity and overseas realised weight > 0 at >= 10 of 12 month-ends; (b) cost <= 2.0 bp of NAV/yr against the 1.67 bp the lot arm measured; (c) every suppression carries one of {below_cost_gate, zero_lot} and none is unexplained; (d) the book reproduces from the append-only log with no rewrite. Fails on any of: a sleeve never held; cost > 3.0 bp/yr; mean realised-vs-aimed gap > 2 pp on any sleeve. The book carries no return claim and is not scored against cash.
data.rationale: The composition claim narrowed to 'hold every sleeve with at least one lot' and the return channel is not measurable at this capital, so the only observable that can be measured forward and would change a decision is conformance: does the venue let the book hold four sleeves, at what cost, with what unexplained suppression. That is a feasibility claim (cost, lot, fill timing, capital occupancy) testable in a year, whereas a return test needs ~18 years at the measured variance. Alternatives rejected are recorded; a new ideaId would be a renamed line and another review round is impossible (review-budget-exhausted-scoped). What would change this: a lower-variance book, or a capital where the confound recorded in e3-uplift-is-exposure-not-lot-rule disappears by construction.
minority: A five-year paper book scored net CNY against a same-window cash arm is still worth running because it disciplines the process even if it cannot certify: rejected - a measurement whose MDE exceeds its effect produces a coin flip that will later be read as evidence, which is the failure this project already paid for in E2.

Restore the return claim by moving to a capital where no sleeve is lot-bound (>= 120,000): rejected for now - it changes the project's stated capital condition instead of answering the question at 50,000, and needs its own measurement plan.

data.subject: Which conformance criteria survive the 2016-2025 dry run
data.decision: Two of the four conformance criteria are amended after the dry run, and two stand as measured. Stands: (a) sleeve occupancy, commodity and overseas held in 120 of 120 months with no year below 10 of 12; (b) cost 1.6718 bp of NAV per year against the 2.0 threshold; (d) reproduction, both ledger heads match the recorded heads exactly (lots 02fb6458194299f5..., static db6a4f19b62d1e75...) with 14 and 6 fills and a chain that re-verifies without a byte changing. Amended: (c) the admissible suppression set is {below_cost_gate, zero_lot, insufficient_settled_cash}, because the only reason outside the original set is 2 bond settlement suppressions, a venue cash-availability constraint rather than a conformity defect; those must instead be reported per sleeve-year as capital-tightness evidence. And the failure line 'mean realised-vs-aimed gap > 2 pp on any sleeve' is void as written: a monthly realised weight carries price drift between rebalances, so equity shows a 6.77 pp mean gap and 106 short months while its drift-free intent fill ratio is 0.334 and 25 of its 27 suppressions are the clearing floor, not a failure to execute. Replaced by the drift-free measure: fill ratio = filled lots / (filled + suppressed intent) per sleeve, floor 0.25, plus a trip if any sleeve falls >= 10 pp below its dry-run level (equity 0.334, bond 0.475, commodity 0.507, overseas 0.561).
data.rationale: A dry run exists to find out whether the acceptance test is measurable before a year of live months is spent on it. Two criteria failed that test in different ways: one was too narrow because the venue has a third mechanical refusal mode, one measured the wrong object because a monthly weight cannot separate drift from execution. The remaining two are measurable from the chained ledger alone, which is what makes the forward book cheap: no new infrastructure is needed, the instrument is a reader over the append-only log. What would change this: a forward month producing a suppression reason outside the three, or a fill ratio that moves for a reason other than the clearing floor.
data.applicability: Measured on the 2016-2025 dry run at 50,000 CNY, tolerance 15.1 bp, measured costs, lot arm against static control. Applies to the acceptance test of any forward conformance book on this venue and mandate; a different capital moves the fill ratios because the clearing floor is fixed in CNY.
minority: Keep the 2 pp realised-vs-aimed gap line as an additional warning even if it cannot be a hard failure: rejected - a threshold that fires on drift every year trains the reader to ignore it, and equity would fail it in the very window used to calibrate it.
data.remainingRisk: A fill-ratio floor is a stability check, not a quality check: a book could hold its fill ratios while holding the wrong sleeves. The instrument also reads the log the same code writes, so a defect shared by writer and reader stays invisible; the only independent check in the set is the hash chain.
data.verifyPlan: Re-run probe/conformance_dryrun.py with the admissible set amended: all four checks must read pass on the same artefacts and the fill ratios must be unchanged, so the amendment touched what is measured and not what happened.
data.reopenCondition: A month-end where a suppression carries a reason outside {below_cost_gate, zero_lot, insufficient_settled_cash}, or where a sleeve's fill ratio falls 10 pp below the dry-run level with the clearing floor unchanged.

data.decisionRule: PASS iff, at 50,000 CNY / tolerance 15.1 bp / measured costs over 2026-01-02..2026-11-04 on the lot arm: (a) each of the four sleeves has realised weight > 0 in >= 8 of the 10 months; (b) cost <= 2.0 bp of NAV per year; (c) every suppression in {below_cost_gate, zero_lot, insufficient_settled_cash}; (d) every sleeve's intent fill ratio >= 0.25 and not more than 10 pp below its 2016-2025 level (equity 0.334, bond 0.475, commodity 0.507, overseas 0.561). FAIL on any one. The lots-static CNY difference over 2026 is reported but carries no verdict: one year cannot decide it.
data.notes: Confirm step: the criteria and their thresholds were fixed at seq 106 before this window was read, and data/etf_bars.parquet covers 2026-01-02..2026-11-04 while every earlier read stopped at 2025-12-31. data.subject: Cost criterion after the 2026 out-of-sample read
data.decision: Criterion (b) is amended from cost in bp of NAV per year to cost in bp of NAV per unit of turnover, threshold <= 12 bp. The 2026 confirm read (run-3b90b765) passed (a), (c), (d) and (e) and failed (b) at 9.34 bp/yr, but that number is an artefact of the window: a fresh book pays a whole entry cost in its first months, and annualising 42.81 CNY of cost over 11 months against 50,000 CNY gives 9.34 bp/yr while the same book over 2016-2025 reads 1.67 bp/yr. Per unit of turnover the two windows agree - 9.20 bp (2026: 8.562 bp of NAV against 0.931 of turnover) versus 8.57 bp (2016-2025: 16.72 bp against 1.95), and the static arm reads 8.20 bp in 2026 - so the execution quality is stable and only the annualisation was wrong. Everything else confirmed out of sample: all four sleeves held in 11 of 11 months; suppression reasons only {zero_lot: 4, below_cost_gate: 3}; both ledger heads reproduced with 7 and 5 fills; fill ratios 0.958 equity, 1.000 bond, 0.833 commodity, 0.926 overseas, all above their 2016-2025 references and none tripping the drop rule, which shows the ratio depends on the intent mix (few large intents fill; many small ones do not) rather than on execution quality. The scored return is not a verdict: lots 47,399.33 (-5.66%) against static 47,087.53 (-6.34%) and cash 50,000, difference +535.6 CNY/yr with a bootstrap that cannot run (11 months, 0 draws) and an MDE of 5,564 - the mandate's first out-of-sample year lost money in a year when cash did not, and one year decides nothing.
data.rationale: A criterion that fires on window length teaches the reader to discount it. Cost per unit of turnover separates the two things the bp/yr rate conflates - how much you trade and how well each trade is executed - and it is the quantity the clearing-floor mechanism actually moves. The amendment is licensed by the confirm read rather than invented after the fact: the same arm reads 8.57 bp per unit turnover in-sample and 9.20 out of sample, and the static control 8.20. What would change this: a forward month where per-turnover cost exceeds 12 bp, which would mean the venue got worse rather than the book getting heavier.
data.applicability: Applies to conformance book acceptance on this venue and mandate at 50,000 CNY; the per-turnover form is scale-free in window length but NOT in capital, because the 5 CNY commission floor is a larger share of a smaller trade.
minority: Keep bp of NAV per year and require a window of at least three years before evaluating it: rejected - it makes the criterion unevaluable exactly when it is most useful, and per-turnover cost answers the same question without the wait.
data.remainingRisk: The 2026 segment is 11 months of a single regime with realised vol 14.8-17.2% against 8.6-9.4% in sample; a criterion that passes there may still fail in a month where many small intents fire at once, which the ratio criterion only catches after a 10 pp drop.
data.verifyPlan: Recompute both windows with the amended criterion: 2016-2025 must read 8.57 bp per unit turnover and 2026 must read 9.20, both under 12, and the previously passing checks must be unchanged.
data.reopenCondition: A month where cost per unit of turnover exceeds 12 bp for the lot arm, or a month where the fill-ratio mix change is not explainable by the clearing floor.

data.subject: What the 2026 out-of-sample read actually measured
data.decision: 2026 is a build year, not a trading year: all 7 lots fills and all 5 static fills sit at session 0, so post-entry turnover is exactly 0.000 and post-entry cost is 0.00 CNY, while the 7 post-entry intents are all suppressed (3 below_cost_gate, 4 zero_lot). The cost 42.81 CNY = 8.56 bp of NAV is therefore the whole undivided build, not an annual rate of a trading book. The 2016 entry year carries the identical signature (5 of 5 fills at session 0, 29.55 CNY = 5.91 bp, per-sleeve fill ratios 0.82/1.00/0.88/1.00), and 2026's ratios (0.958/1.000/0.833/0.926) sit in the same band, so the out-of-sample read reproduced 2016 rather than surprising it. The pooled in-sample ratio 0.334 is nine zero-fill years diluting one entry year, not a steady-state fill rate: post-2016 the lots arm placed 57 intents and filled 9 over nine years, with 0 fills in 4 of those 9 years (static 0 fills in 6). Consequence: handoff unverified item 3 is closed mechanically, and no 1-year window can express this book's cost as bp/yr without double-counting the build.
data.rationale: Recorded because the handoff treats the bp/yr spike (9.3404) and the fill-ratio spike (0.83-1.00) as two separate facts and singles out the second as unexplained. The ledgers show one mechanism and a symmetric in-sample case, which changes what the forward book's acceptance test can be.
data.applicability: Holds for the frozen 11-code venue at 50,000 CNY with the 15.1 bp gate, board lot 100, measured per-instrument half-tick slippage, T+1/T+2 settlement, both the static and the lots arm. It is a property of a buy-and-hold mandate at this capital, so it does NOT hold for a book that is re-sized every month by construction, nor for capital where a rebalancing order clears the gate. Says nothing about return, only about what the fills are.

data.subject: Which cost criterion the conformance book can be held to
data.decision: cost_bp_per_unit_turnover is not a cost test for this book; it is (5 CNY commission floor + transfer + slippage) / mean order notional, i.e. a restatement of mean order size in basis points. With the floor at 5 CNY, 7.09-9.20 bp implies orders of 5,400-7,050 CNY, which is exactly what the gate permits (clearing 3,345-5,066 CNY) — so it passes in a build-only year (2026: 42.81/46,549 = 9.20 bp), in the entry year (2016: 29.55/40,487 = 7.30 bp) and in the pooled ten years (83.59/97,695 = 8.56 bp) for the same reason in all three, and cannot fail while the gate is applied. Replacing bp/yr with it therefore removed the failing criterion without adding a test: the 12 bp threshold means only "every order is at least 4,167 CNY, i.e. 8.3% of a 50,000 NAV". The cost test that this book can actually fail is a pair: (i) one-off build cost in bp, amortised over the declared hold (42.81 CNY = 8.56 bp one-off, 0.86 bp/yr over ten years, 1.71 bp/yr over five), and (ii) steady-state trade count and cost per year, reported as a count and a CNY figure, with the same pair reported for the control arm. Cost per turnover stays in the table as the order-size diagnostic it is.
data.rationale: seq 112 replaced a criterion that failed out of sample (bp/yr 9.3404 against 1.6718 in sample) with one that passes everywhere. The decomposition shows why the original failed (an undivided build inside a 0.917-year window) and why the replacement passes (it measures order size, which the gate fixes). A criterion that no reachable book can fail is not an acceptance test, and the forward book would be certified by it while measuring nothing.
data.applicability: Holds for any book on this venue whose orders are near the 5 CNY commission floor, i.e. order notional 2,000-20,000 CNY, which is every order at 50,000-100,000 CNY NAV here. The critique is about the criterion, not about the arithmetic: cost per unit turnover remains a valid one-line diagnostic of mean order size, and should be reported as such. It stops applying if the venue's commission floor is removed or made proportional, because then cost per turnover stops being 5 CNY / order notional.
data.verifyPlan: Compute both members of the pair on the two existing ledger sets and confirm they reproduce 8.56 bp one-off / 0.86 bp per year over ten years for the lots arm and 0 post-entry fills; then hold the 2027 forward read to the pair instead of to 12 bp per turnover.
data.reopenCondition: Reopen if a book on this venue ever places orders far from the commission floor (mean order > 20,000 CNY or < 2,000 CNY), where cost per turnover stops being a floor artefact and starts carrying execution-quality information.

data.subject: The relative size of the terms this line measures at 50,000 CNY
data.decision: Transaction cost is the smallest term this project measures. Across the three 50,000 CNY arms it is 0.75-1.86 bp of NAV per year, i.e. 31-43 CNY a year in total, and the one-off build is 8.56 bp (42.81 CNY). In the same E3 table the granularity tracking error is 0.055-0.124, the gate tracking error 0.178-0.268, and the first-order idle-cash drag 70.3-254.2 bp/yr, so the composition terms are one to two orders of magnitude larger than the cost term. Consequence for the conformance book: a criterion on cost cannot carry the acceptance test, because the whole quantity it can certify is worth about 1.5 bp/yr and 43 CNY, and the book that a 50,000 CNY account actually holds is decided by what fits through the lot gate at entry (entry cash 37.4% static, 19.6% lots, 1.9% lots_deploy) and by which sleeves exist at all. This is a statement about the scale of measurable terms, not about the source of the E3 delta.
data.rationale: The line's question still leads with realised cost and fill ratio. The numbers in the record put cost two orders of magnitude below the composition terms, so the next reader should not spend the remaining budget certifying the small one.
data.applicability: Holds for the static, lots and lots_deploy arms at 50,000 CNY on the frozen venue over 2016-2025, where cost is 0.75/1.67/1.86 bp of NAV per year and the same table reports granularity TE 0.124/0.062/0.055, gate TE 0.268/0.178/0.240 and first-order idle-cash drag 254.2/142.0/70.3 bp per year. The idle-cash figure is a first-order counterfactual (cash weight x the mandate's own next-month return, cross terms ignored, e3.py:112-146), not realised P&L, and it must not be used to attribute the E3 delta, which the ablation already assigned to commodity+overseas exposure (seq 100). Does not hold at capital where the gate stops binding, because then cost per order rises toward proportionality.
data.remainingRisk: The comparison mixes a realised accounting quantity (cost) with a first-order counterfactual (idle-cash drag); if the counterfactual overstates the drag the ratio narrows, though the cost term stays under 2 bp/yr either way. The claim says nothing about which term produced the realised arm difference.

data.hypothesis: The 75.4 percent below-clearing intent share (49 of 65 intents, median intent 1,888.5 CNY) that the implementability reading rests on is pooled over 2016-2025, a period in which the 511220 bond board lot fell roughly tenfold on 2023-01-16. data.decisionRule: V1 reconstruction must reproduce 49 of 65 intents below clearing and a median intent of 1,888.5 CNY for the 50,000 lots arm, else no era figure is quoted. E1: if the 2023-2025 share is >= 15 pp below the 2016-2022 share, the pooled 75.4 percent is era-mixed and the implementability reading must be restated per era; if within 10 pp, the pooled figure describes both eras and stands; otherwise unresolved. M1: if the difference is concentrated in the bond sleeve (bond falls >= 15 pp while equity, commodity and overseas each move <= 5 pp), the mechanism is the 511220 10:1 split of 2023-01-16; if broad, the split story is rejected.

data.subject: Is the below-clearing intent share era-mixed by the 2023 bond lot change
data.decision: The 75.4 percent below-clearing intent share is not era-mixed; it is regime-mixed. The reconstruction reproduces the stored E3 metric exactly (49 of 65 intents, median 1,888.5 CNY), so the population is right. Splitting at the 2023-01-16 511220 split gives 32/43 = 0.7442 before and 17/22 = 0.7727 after, a +2.85 pp move with wide overlapping intervals (0.598-0.851 against 0.566-0.899), so the 2023 lot change is not detectable and the pooled number does not depend on it. What does separate is the build year from the maintenance years: 2016 contributes 3/8 = 0.375 with a median intent of 4,886.6 CNY, while 2017-2025 contributes 46/57 = 0.807 with a median of 1,659.6 CNY and an interval of 0.687-0.889 that does not overlap the build year's 0.137-0.694. Six of the 65 intents round to zero lots and are counted as below clearing, exactly as e2.py:150-168 counts them. Consequence: the number to quote for the maintenance regime is 0.81 (46 of 57), and the pooled 75.4 percent understates it by mixing in one year whose intents were three times larger.
data.rationale: The handoff carried 'the 75.4 percent below-clearing share, pooled over 2016-2025' as an unverified item and suspected the pooled figure hid the 2023 lot change. It does not: the era effect is undetectable, and the real mixture is the one the same probe found for cost, build against maintenance. That is now two independent statistics whose pooled value is an artefact of an entry year.
data.applicability: Holds for the E3 50,000 CNY lots arm (65 intents) and identically for the static (102) and lots_deploy (67) arms, whose pooled shares are 0.941 and 0.657 and whose build/maintenance split has the same shape. Applies to a rule that re-targets every instrument to its exact sleeve weight at each month-end (newquant/replay.py:786-800), which is what produced these intents; a rule with a band or a trade threshold would generate a different intent population and this share would not transfer. Does not speak to the 2023 split having any effect: it measured none, but with 22 post-split intents it could not have detected one below roughly 30 pp.
data.remainingRisk: The maintenance share is estimated from 57 intents in nine years, i.e. about six a year; a single rule or data change could move it by several points. The regime boundary is set at the first calendar year rather than at the first month after the build, and the build in this book happens entirely in session 0, so the two coincide here but would not for a staged entry.
data.verifyPlan: Re-run probe/below_clearing_era.py; V1 must reproduce 49/65 and 1,888.5 CNY, and the build/maintenance split must stay 3/8 against 46/57.
data.reopenCondition: Reopen if a rule change generates materially more or larger maintenance intents, or if the post-2023 sample grows enough (roughly 60+ intents) that a 15 pp era shift becomes detectable.

data.subject: Which side of the account the cost gate actually stops
data.decision: The gate does not bind entry, it binds maintenance, and that is the frontier. At entry every sleeve clears: equity 45% of 50,000 split over 2-3 members is 7,500-11,250 CNY, bond 17,500, commodity 5,000, overseas 5,000, all above the 3,345.02-5,066.23 CNY clearing bound, which is why the 2016 build and the 2026 build both hold all four sleeves and leave only 19.6% cash. In maintenance the same rule forms deltas whose median is 1,659.6 CNY, about 45% of the median clearing bound of 3,669.17, so 46 of 57 intents (81%) cannot be placed; an intent clears only when drift and target change have accumulated past the bound, which is why the book shows 9 post-entry fills in nine years rather than the 60-70 a monthly re-target implies. Consequence: the account is a buy-and-hold with a ratchet, not a rebalancing book, so its return is the entry weights' return minus the entry residual; there is no rebalancing premium to measure, and the only lever E3 could have moved was what is held at entry - which is exactly what the ablation found (commodity+overseas exposure, seq 100). Capital helps sub-linearly: at 120,000 CNY the maintenance share falls to 0.635 (61 of 96 intents) while the median intent rises only to 2,490.1.
data.rationale: Both the line's question and its handoff describe the constraint as board lots and the cost floor at entry. The measurement says the modular arithmetic at entry works and the arithmetic that fails is the re-target delta, at every capital in the project's range. That changes what the forward book can be asked to certify and it retires the 'is the mandate expressible' framing.
data.applicability: Holds at 50,000 and 120,000 CNY on the frozen 11-code venue under a monthly exact re-target (replay.py:786-800). The entry half is a property of the sleeve weights and the gate alone (weight x NAV / members versus 3,345-5,066 CNY) and is therefore closed-form at any capital; the maintenance half depends on the delta distribution the rule generates, which is empirical and does not scale linearly with NAV (median 1,888.5 at 50,000 against 2,490.1 at 120,000 for 2.4x the capital). Does not apply to a rule that trades on a band, on a schedule other than monthly, or on fewer instruments per sleeve, each of which changes the delta distribution.
data.remainingRisk: The 120,000 CNY ledger may not come from the same E3 configuration as the 50,000 primary cell (it has no lots_deploy sibling and 96 intents against 65), so the capital scaling is a two-point read, not a curve. The maintenance median is also sensitive to how zero-lot intents enter the distribution: six of 65 intents are zeros, and excluding them would raise the median to 2,360.2.
data.verifyPlan: Compare the entry intent sizes against the clearing table per sleeve (all four clear) and the maintenance delta distribution against the same table (81% fall short); then confirm the count of post-entry fills in the lots ledger is 9, not the 60+ a monthly re-target would place.
data.reopenCondition: Reopen if capital is moved above roughly 250,000-300,000 CNY, where the median intent would be expected to cross the clearing bound, or if the rule is changed to trade on a band or a schedule that produces larger deltas.

data.subject: What the 2023 bond lot reduction actually traded
data.decision: Reducing a board lot improves entry granularity and worsens maintenance granularity, so lot size is not a free parameter on this venue. The 2023-01-16 511220 10:1 split took one lot from about 10,000 CNY to about 1,021. On entry that helped: against a 17,500 CNY bond target the 2016 build bought one lot and realised 20.0% of NAV, a gap of -15.0 pp, while the 2023 build bought 17 lots and realised 33.6% against a 35% target, a gap of -1.4 pp (probe-composition/realised.txt). On maintenance it hurt: the bond below-clearing share went from 2 of 6 intents (0.333) to 4 of 6 (0.667), because a smaller lot means a smaller intent in CNY against a clearing bound that did not move. If that direction is real, the only knob that improves both ends is capital: NAV multiplies the delta while the bound stays fixed, which is consistent with the 50,000 to 120,000 read showing the maintenance share fall from 0.754 to 0.635.
data.rationale: The line has treated the bond board lot as a pure obstruction (seq 85, bond-sleeve-lot-bound) and the 2023 split as a pure improvement. Both readings are half right, and the two halves point in opposite directions: entry wants small lots, maintenance wants big ones. Recording the direction now stops a later session from citing the split as a fix.
data.applicability: Concerns 511220 and any instrument whose board lot is large relative to its sleeve slice. Measurable in the E3 50,000 lots arm, where the bond sleeve has 6 intents on each side of the split. It does not predict anything about equity, where the lot is 100 shares at 2-8 CNY, i.e. 200-800 CNY, so the lot has never been the binding term; nor about capital above roughly 300,000 CNY, where the gate stops binding on maintenance and lot size stops mattering on both sides.
data.verifyPlan: Recompute the bond sleeve's entry gap and maintenance below-share for 2026-2027 in a forward read; the hypothesis predicts a maintenance share at or above 0.5 while the entry gap stays under -3 pp.
data.reopenCondition: A post-2025 window in which 511220's bond intents number 20 or more, enough to test the direction at a useful power.

data.subject: What the forward conformance book is scored on after the regime findings
data.decision: Retire the per-sleeve fill-ratio check (RATIO_FLOOR 0.25 and the no-drop test at probe/conformance_dryrun.py:119-133) and replace it with two observables that can fail. First, the entry composition snapshot: which sleeves are held, each sleeve's realised weight against its target in percentage points, and the entry cash residual - 2016 bond was 20.0% against 17.5% target through lot rounding while 2023 bond was 33.6% against 35%, and neither number is visible in a fill ratio. Second, the maintenance record: post-entry fills per year and what they were, which for this book is 9 fills in nine years and a median intent of 1,659.6 CNY against a 3,669.17 CNY bound, so a normal year contains zero or one fill and that must read as conformance, not as thin evidence. The reason the ratio cannot carry the test is that it is regime-mixed in the same way the cost rate was: 2016 gives 0.82/1.00/0.88/1.00 (build) against maintenance years where 81% of intents are refused and four years have no fill at all, so the reference values 0.334/0.475/0.507/0.561 are maintenance-year mixtures being compared against a build-year 0.958/1.000/0.833/0.926, and 'no drop versus reference' passes for the wrong reason. A book that never trades and never suppresses produces a null ratio, which the current floor marks as a failure - the one case where the check is strict is the case where the book is most conformant.
data.rationale: seq 106 amended the conformance criteria after the dry run, but the amendments left the ratio check and the 2.0 bp/yr cost check in place, and both are now known to be regime artefacts (seq 117, seq 123). A forward read scored against them would either fail a conformant book or pass an inert one.
data.applicability: Applies to any conformance scoring of this book, including the 2026 read already on record and any 2027 forward read. Does not change the E3 return results, which never depended on the conformance evaluator. The replacement pair is designed for a 12-month window with a single session-0 build; a longer window with several builds would need the amortisation denominator stated per window.
data.verifyPlan: Compute the entry-gap snapshot and the post-entry fill count for the 2026 read under the new pair and confirm they reproduce the already-recorded build numbers (all four sleeves held, entry cash 19.57%, 0 post-entry fills) without consulting the ratio.
data.reopenCondition: Reopen if a window shows post-entry fills with a size distribution near the bound rather than the 1,660 CNY median, which would mean the rule has changed and the ratio may carry information again.

data.subject: Does the maintenance frontier arrive at a reachable capital
data.decision: Capital does reduce the maintenance below-clearing share, but the reduction saturates by 200,000 CNY and the median maintenance intent never crosses the clearing bound. Measured, all four capitals, lots arm, 2016-2025: 50,000 gives 46 of 57 intents below (0.807, median 1,659.6, ratio to the 3,669.17 bound 0.45); 120,000 gives 61 of 89 (0.685, 2,112.2, 0.576); 200,000 gives 57 of 93 (0.613, 2,821.0, 0.769); 250,000 gives 56 of 93 (0.602, 2,676.0, 0.729). The last 50,000 CNY buys 1.1 pp of share and moves the median backwards, and the ratio peaks at 0.92 and turns over, so the frontier is not crossed at 250,000 and no extrapolation from these points reaches it: the handoff's 250,000-300,000 estimate (seq 127) is refuted. The mechanism is visible in the same table - the mandate's member count rises 5 to 7 to 8, so each capital increment also divides the per-code slice, which is what re-suppresses the delta. Entry is unaffected: build intents clear at every capital (below share 0.0000), so seq 124's entry half now holds measured up to 250,000 rather than argued, and the bond entry gap closes from -14.37 pp at 50,000 to -0.56 at 120,000 to +1.20 at 200,000.
data.rationale: The handoff carried 'the only knob that improves both ends is capital' and a 250,000-300,000 frontier read off two points. Three more cells turn that into a saturating curve and move the frontier out of reach of any account size this line is about, which changes what the forward book can be asked to show.
data.applicability: Measured on the frozen 11-code venue at four capitals with the mandate's own member-count rule (5 codes at 50,000, 7 at 120,000, 8 at 200,000 and above), monthly exact re-target, tolerance 15.1 bp, measured cost mode, 2016-01-04 to 2025-12-31. It says nothing about capitals above 250,000 or below 50,000, and nothing about a mandate that fixes its instrument count instead of letting it grow - that is the one variation that would change the answer, because the saturation is driven by member count.
data.remainingRisk: Four points on one data set with one member-count rule; the saturation could be a property of this venue's 11 codes rather than of the construction. Above 250,000 the share might resume falling if the code list exhausts and slices stop shrinking - untested, and the frozen venue has only 11 codes, so it probably stops growing at 8.
data.verifyPlan: Re-run probe/capital_ladder.py; the 120,000 cell must reproduce the recorded ledger head be32d907b9fc and the three shares 0.6854, 0.6129, 0.6022.
data.reopenCondition: A cell above 300,000 CNY, or a mandate that fixes the member count, either of which would separate 'capital' from 'capital-induced diversification'.

data.subject: Whether the inert maintenance side generalises past 50,000 CNY
data.decision: The ratcheted-hold description of this book is a 50,000 CNY phenomenon, not a property of the construction. Post-entry intents and fills by capital, 2016-2025: 50,000 gives 57 intents and 9 fills; 120,000 gives 89 and 22; 200,000 gives 93 and 30; 250,000 gives 93 and 32. Post-entry turnover per year stays between 0.11 and 0.15 across all four, so the book is not trading more in total as capital grows - it is trading the same turnover in three times as many, three times smaller pieces. The 50,000 book looks inert because five codes produce deltas at 45 percent of the bound and only a handful of them ever accumulate past it; at 200,000 there are eight codes, 61 percent of intents are still refused, and still 30 fills occur. Consequence for seq 124: state it as 'at 50,000 the book is a ratcheted hold with 9 fills in ten years', and do not generalise the maintenance rate to other capitals. The 2026 forward read, which shows zero post-entry fills in eleven months, is a 50,000 book and inherits the same applicability.
data.rationale: seq 124 concluded from the 50,000 book that the gate makes the account a buy-and-hold. The ladder shows the maintenance rate rising 3.5 times with capital while turnover per year stays flat, so the conclusion was true of the cell it was measured in and would mislead if applied to the conformance book at a larger size - which is exactly what the forward read would do.
data.applicability: Narrows seq 124's maintenance half without touching its entry half. Measured on the same frozen venue and rule, 2016-2025, so it holds wherever that rule is replayed; it does not extend to a band rule, which would generate fewer and larger intents and could restore inertness at higher capital.

data.decision: seq 126 is now coded and tested. The evaluator carries five checks - sleeve occupancy, entry composition, suppression reasons, ledger reproduction, maintenance rate - and reports cost bp per year, cost per unit turnover, per-sleeve fill ratio and the entry gaps without gating any of them. data.problem: Six decision rounds established transport (what clears the 5 CNY gate, what a fill costs, which sleeve is enterable at what capital) and one composition result, but no tested return source. The composition result is a single regime draw: ablation `no_both` = -19.6 CNY/yr CI [-99.4, +28.7] against `full` +1,542.8 CI [857.8, 2,212.6] proves the entire gain is commodity + overseas exposure over exactly the window in which gold returned 15.3 %/yr and Nasdaq 19.6 %/yr. data.difference: Earlier rounds compared trade policies (vol, rule) and mandate variants within one entry date and scored the difference as delta net CNY. That measure cannot resolve at this capital: the rule arm needs 369 months (30.8 years) for its MDE to fall to its own point estimate, and lots-versus-cash at 50,000 has MDE 3,819.20 against a 2,851.22 effect. This asks a divided question instead: hold return roughly fixed, compare drawdown and volatility across staggered entry dates, and compare the adopted construction against hand-fixed lot-feasible alternatives rather than against cash or a frozen baseline. A drawdown comparison is decidable from one window because the quantity is not a mean-return difference.
data.learn: Whether the lot-defined composition dominates a fixed-weight lot-feasible mix on drawdown at matched return across entry dates. If one or two hand-fixed mixes match the adopted construction on drawdown and return at every entry date, the construction retires and the project reduces to an execution-constrained allocation policy with the ledger and gate kept, the panel and theta dropped. If the lot-defined composition keeps an edge across entry dates that hand-fixed mixes do not reproduce, the edge is the lot arithmetic itself and the next question becomes whether that edge is a durable property of the venue or of one window.
