data.subject: What is the per-start ordering band width, and what does the one available pre-window rule cost?
data.decision: Per-start band widths, not the spread of means, are the measurement the account's rule must be priced against. Per start (base regime, six orderings, 50 000 CNY) the gap-to-hold range is 1.340 / 2.280 / 1.537 / 2.023 / 1.675 / 1.742 pp/yr for starts 2016-01-04 / 2017-04-05 / 2018-07-02 / 2020-01-02 / 2021-10-08 / 2023-10-09, mean 1.766. The 1.743 pp/yr figure used earlier is the spread of the six ordering MEANS and is not any start's width; the two coincide only because the mean width happens to be 1.766. The only pre-window member rule on record (median turnover over the prior 120 sessions, which names 159920) sits at the WORST edge of the band at all six starts, so its per-start regret against the best ordering equals the full per-start width: 1.340 / 2.280 / 1.537 / 2.023 / 1.675 / 1.742, mean 1.766 pp/yr, worst 2.280.
data.rationale: Answers direction-review objection R2 (round round-536c2b7a), which caught the substitution of an aggregate range for a per-start width. Also reframes R3: a rule cannot be accepted by being 'inside the band', because a rule that names one benchmark path is inside it by construction; the measurable thing is regret against the best ordering at each start, and on this window the one rule on record takes the maximum.
data.remainingRisk: The band is computed from the six ex-post orderings, so 'regret against the best ordering' is an ex-post benchmark; a rule can only be judged against it, never tuned to it, and the six starts are the same ones the band came from.
data.verifyPlan: Recompute from summary.json cells.base[t][s].gap_pp_yr whenever the grid changes; the six widths are exactly max-min within each start.

data.subject: Does Baule 2010 treat asset identity as a decision variable, and by what mechanism?
data.decision: Baule 2010 chooses asset IDENTITY by optimization, so the ordering question does not arise there for a structural reason, not a missing one. Verified in the body, PDF p8 (printed p6): "if the set of assets with strictly positive weights in the portfolio is fixed, the transaction cost function is convex and thus classical portfolio selection on this subset of assets can be performed. Hence, a theoretical approach to solve the optimization problem would be to conduct a classical portfolio selection for each of the 2^n possible subsets" (footnote 6 cites Lobo/Fazel/Boyd 2007 p.353). So his model's identity of the held assets is a decision variable resolved by exhaustive subset selection over 2^n with continuous weights inside each subset, and the capital-to-cardinality map of p21 Table 2 (n* = 1/2/3/6/14 at 1k/5k/10k/50k/100k EUR) is that optimizer's output, not a tie-break. The engine here resolves identity by the order of SLEEVE_MEMBERS, which no criterion sets, and cannot optimize because at 50 000 CNY one member of the overseas sleeve fits at all.
data.rationale: Answers direction-review objection R1 (round round-536c2b7a), which held that 'absence of a lot constraint does not imply absence of a member-selection problem'. The reviewer is right that fixed costs make identity consequential inside Baule - and Baule settles it by 2^n subset enumeration. What the engine lacks is therefore not the known mechanism but any statement of what replaces the optimizer when the optimizer's answer is unavailable at this capital.
data.remainingRisk: Reading one page settles what Baule's model does with identity, not whether some later fixed-cost paper already proposes a rule for the case where only one asset fits. The negative search for that is still only a negative search.
data.verifyPlan: Read Baule's numerical section (printed pp13-18) for how the 2^n enumeration is made tractable, and check whether he reports the identity of the selected assets at each capital level.

data.subject: Per-start ordering band widths and the regret of the one available pre-window rule
data.decision: Per-start band widths, not the spread of ordering means, price the account's member rule: 1.340 / 2.280 / 1.537 / 2.023 / 1.675 / 1.742 pp/yr across the six starts, mean 1.766. The only pre-window rule on record (median turnover over the prior 120 sessions, naming 159920) sits at the worst edge of every band, so its per-start regret against the best ordering equals the full width at 6/6 starts, mean 1.766, worst 2.280 pp/yr.
data.rationale: Supersedes the same finding recorded without applicability at seq 222, which the state view kept as a hypothesis. Answers R2 and reframes R3 from round round-536c2b7a.
data.applicability: 50 000 CNY, overseas sleeve, six starts 2016-01-04/2017-04-05/2018-07-02/2020-01-02/2021-10-08/2023-10-09, base regime (tol 15.1 bp, floor max(gate, one lot), measured cost); gap convention hold@200 divided by lots annualised, so positive means the lots arm trails hold. Widths are ex-post and are not usable as a tuning target.
data.remainingRisk: The band is ex post and comes from the same six starts the rule would be judged on.
data.verifyPlan: max-min of cells.base[t][s].gap_pp_yr within each start in evidence/probe-constraint-control/summary.json.
data.reopenCondition: A start whose band width is zero, which would mean the ordering freedom is absent there.

data.subject: Baule's treatment of asset identity, verified in the body
data.decision: Baule 2010 resolves asset identity by optimization - exhaustive classical selection over each of the 2^n subsets ("if the set of assets with strictly positive weights in the portfolio is fixed, the transaction cost function is convex and thus classical portfolio selection on this subset of assets can be performed ... a theoretical approach ... would be to conduct a classical portfolio selection for each of the 2^n possible subsets", PDF p8 / printed p6, footnote citing Lobo/Fazel/Boyd 2007 p.353). So fixed costs do make identity consequential in his model, and his n* map (1/2/3/6/14 at 1k/5k/10k/50k/100k EUR) is that optimizer's output. The engine here has no optimizer and no stated replacement: identity comes from the order of SLEEVE_MEMBERS, and at 50 000 CNY only one overseas member fits at all.
data.rationale: Supersedes seq 223, recorded without applicability and therefore held as a hypothesis. Answers R1 from round round-536c2b7a on the body rather than on a summary: the reviewer's claim that fixed costs already make identity consequential is correct, and Baule settles it by 2^n enumeration, which is exactly the instrument the account lacks at this capital.
data.applicability: Baule 2010 OR Spectrum 32:61-76 as printed; the 2^n enumeration is on PDF p8 (printed p6) and the cardinality results on p21 Table 2. Applies to models with continuous holdings and per-order fixed fees; says nothing about integral lots or about a tie-break rule.
data.remainingRisk: One page establishes what Baule's model does; whether a later paper already prescribes a rule for the case where only one asset fits is still only a negative search.
data.verifyPlan: Read printed pp13-18 for whether the selected identities are reported per capital level; if they are, the account's rule can be compared with his optimizer's choice directly.
data.reopenCondition: A source prescribing a member rule for the single-asset-feasible case under a per-order fee.

data.subject: Which pre-window criteria separate the three overseas funds, and what does each cost?
data.decision: Every liquidity, price and age criterion names 159920 and lands on the worst ordering at 6/6 starts, while trailing 12-month return names 513100 at 5/6. Medians of daily amount over the prior 120 sessions (10k CNY): at 2016-01-04 159920 1 765.7 vs 513100 208.4 vs 513500 113.5; at 2023-10-09 159920 49 978 vs 513100 36 961 vs 513500 15 661. Lowest price and earliest listing also pick 159920 (listed 2013-01-04, before 513100 2013-05-15 and 513500 2014-01-15). The resulting per-start regret against the best ordering: 159920-first mean 1.766 worst 2.280; 513500-first mean 0.440 worst 0.868; 513100-first mean 0.023 worst 0.136 - and 513100-first is best or within 0.136 pp at five of six starts. Trailing return picks 513100 at five starts and 513500 at 2021-10-08, whose regret on that start is 0.415 pp.
data.rationale: Answers R3 from round round-536c2b7a by comparing candidate rules instead of comparing one rule to a band, and it needs no new replays: a fixed first member already produces the k=1 path in the existing grid. The result is uncomfortable for the direction - the three liquidity/age criteria, which are the ones a spec would naturally use, all converge on the fund with the worst outcome, so 'admissible rules agree' does not make the choice forced in a useful way.
data.applicability: Six starts 2016-01-04/2017-04-05/2018-07-02/2020-01-02/2021-10-08/2023-10-09, 50 000 CNY, criteria computed from data/etf_bars.parquet strictly before the start date (last 120 sessions of amount, price level, first bar date, trailing 252-session close-to-close return); each rule's cost read off the already-priced base-regime grid, where a fixed first member reproduces the k=1 path because the prefix rule truncates the tuple.
data.remainingRisk: Six starts, one sleeve, one market decade; trailing return is a return-based rule and its success here is indistinguishable from having picked the index that happened to outperform.
data.verifyPlan: Recompute the four criteria from bars strictly before each start and map each choice onto its base-regime tag; the mapping is exact while the prefix rule truncates at k=1.
data.reopenCondition: A criterion computable pre-window that is not return-based and still separates the three funds at these starts.

data.subject: What is the overseas ordering spread actually pricing?
data.decision: The overseas ordering spread is an INDEX-EXPOSURE effect, not a construction artefact: the three members track Nasdaq-100, S&P 500 and the Hang Seng, whose qfq CAGRs over 2017-04-05..2026-11-04 are 19.77 %, 13.42 % and 1.12 % - an 18.65 pp/yr spread between the best and worst underlying. The cost gate decides that the sleeve can hold only one of them, and the tuple order decides which, so the 1.34-2.28 pp/yr per-start band and the 12.6 % terminal-NAV dispersion measure the price of being forced into a single foreign index, not the price of a tie-break rule. This is the same conclusion the first handoff read reached from the other direction: the screen never separated 'the book earns nothing' from 'the book is not the mandate', and the equity sleeve's near-zero CAGRs point the same way.
data.rationale: This is the reading that makes the whole line coherent: the gate creates the choice (dispersion 12.643 % with the gate, 0.000 % without it), and the choice is worth 1.34-2.28 pp/yr per start because the three funds are three different foreign indices, not three implementations of one exposure. It supersedes the framing 'the spread is the price of an unstated tie-break', which treated the members as interchangeable.
data.applicability: Overseas sleeve at 50 000 CNY: 513100 tracks Nasdaq-100, 513500 tracks the S&P 500, 159920 tracks the Hang Seng. qfq CAGR 2017-04-05..2026-11-04: 513100 19.77 %, 513500 13.42 %, 159920 1.12 %. Applies whenever a sleeve can hold only one of its members; the same reading applies to any sleeve whose members track different indices rather than variants of one index.
data.remainingRisk: Index identity is inferred from fund codes and their CAGRs, not from a holdings or benchmark table in this workspace; if one of the three tracks something else, the exposure reading changes while the arithmetic does not.
data.verifyPlan: Check the funds' stated benchmarks from their listing documents or a holdings file in the workspace; if two share a benchmark, their 18.65 pp/yr gap must be an implementation difference instead.
data.reopenCondition: A benchmark or holdings record showing two of the three funds track the same index.

data.subject: Does the lot truncate the bond sleeve, and what does that cost?
data.decision: The bond sleeve is NOT the mirror case: its ordering dispersion is 0.124 % of terminal NAV against 12.643 % for overseas, and its ordering spread is 0.024 pp/yr (511220-first -0.776, 511380-first -0.800) against 1.743 pp/yr. My pre-registered P0 required members_bond = 1 at every composition row and it failed, because the sleeve holds 0, 1 or 2 members depending on the month: 511380 does not exist before 2020-04-07, and once both members are live the floor at a grown NAV clears k=2 (lot_off, which drops the lot term from the floor, produces 0.000 % dispersion - bit-identical orderings). The truncation is therefore NAV-path dependent, which is the already-adopted fact `member-count-is-path-dependent` (seq 198): a capital-only prediction could not have told me whether this sleeve is truncated, so the pre-registration contradicted an adopted fact rather than the engine contradicting me.
data.rationale: This is the first sleeve in the book where the truncation costs almost nothing, and the reason is not that the members are similar - 511220 and 511380 differ by 2.32 pp/yr in CAGR and are different assets (duration versus convertibles) - but that the sleeve is truncated for only part of the decade. It redirects the deliverable: the cost of a single-member sleeve is a function of how much of the decade stays truncated, not of the sleeve's weight or its members' spread alone.
data.applicability: Bond sleeve (511220 ten-year local-government bond ~100 CNY par, 511380 convertible bond, listed 2020-04-07), 50 000 CNY, base regime 15.1 bp, six starts, two orderings, 2016-01-04..2026-11-04.
data.remainingRisk: Six starts; the 0.124 % average hides that the 2016 start can spend years at k=1 while later starts spend none; a longer or differently placed start set could raise it.
data.verifyPlan: Read `cells[bond][tag][start]` in evidence/probe-bond-control/summary.json and count, per month, the members_bond values; a start with k=1 for most months and a large dispersion would reopen it.
data.reopenCondition: A start whose bond sleeve stays at k=1 for most of its life, showing a materially larger dispersion.

data.subject: What does the truncated member count cost, sleeve by sleeve?
data.decision: Mean ordering dispersion of terminal NAV, per cent: equity 0.000, bond 0.124, commodity 0.567, overseas 12.643. The pattern is a 2x2 and it isolates the mechanism: dispersion is near zero in both cells where either condition fails - equity holds every listed member at 50 000 CNY so there is no ordering to be exposed to (its members still differ by 3.68 pp/yr in qfq CAGR: 4.05 / 1.83 / 0.37), and commodity is truncated to one member but its two members track the same Au99.99 (11.94 vs 11.86, spread 0.08). Dispersion is large only where the sleeve is BOTH truncated and made of different exposures: overseas 12.643 % against an 18.65 pp/yr member spread. Bond sits between because it is truncated only before 511380 lists on 2020-04-07, after which the grown NAV clears k=2 - which also shows capital is not the variable, since the same 35 % sleeve costs almost nothing once its second member exists.
data.rationale: This is the form the deliverable needs: the constraint is not expensive per se, it is expensive in proportion to how different a sleeve's members are from each other, and it is cheap if the spec either keeps every member (equity) or names members that share an underlying (commodity). It converts an open research question into a specification rule the account can hold, and it gives the one number the earlier screen lacked - what the unstated choice costs, sleeve by sleeve.
data.applicability: Four sleeves as shipped in newquant/replay.py:57-63, 50 000 CNY, base regime (15.1 bp gate, lot floor, measured costs), every distinct ordering of each sleeve's listed members at six starts 2016-01-04..2026-11-04, terminal NAVs read from 94 replay ledgers under D:/d/tmp/rd_disp.
data.remainingRisk: Six starts, one decade, one market; the 2x2 uses two sleeves per cell at most, and the commodity cell's 0.567 % is single-underlying noise rather than zero by construction.
data.verifyPlan: Recompute the four dispersions from the ledgers under D:/d/tmp/rd_disp; the rebuild is arithmetic over terminal NAVs, so any change in the table means a replay differed.
data.reopenCondition: A sleeve that is truncated and whose members share an underlying yet disperses more than a few per cent, or an untruncated sleeve that disperses.

data.subject: How should the spec name the overseas member at 50 000 CNY?
data.decision: The account should be specified with one NAMED fund per sleeve rather than a member tuple, and for the overseas sleeve that fund is 513100. Reason: a single-member tuple has no ordering, so the 12.643 % dispersion disappears by construction, and pricing the decision shows 513100-first is the best or within 0.136 pp/yr of the best ordering at all six starts (mean regret 0.023 pp/yr), while the criteria a spec would otherwise reach for - median turnover, lowest price, earliest listing - pick 159920 at 6/6 and cost 1.766 pp/yr on average, 2.280 at worst. The commitment is therefore cheap at the best available member and expensive at the "natural" one, which is why the member must be named in the spec instead of left to the engine's tuple order. The honest caveat, recorded rather than hidden: 513100 tracks the Nasdaq-100, whose 19.77 % qfq CAGR over 2017-04-05..2026-11-04 is 16.5 pp/yr above the Hang Seng's 1.12 %, so this naming is an index decision that the past decade happened to reward, not a construction rule that will keep paying.
data.rationale: It is the smallest change that removes the undecidability the line was opened for, it is implementable at 50 000 CNY (one lot of 513100 is about 159 CNY against a 5 000 CNY sleeve), and its cost is measured against the alternatives rather than asserted. Naming the member also makes the residual risk visible as an index bet, which the tuple made invisible.
data.applicability: Overseas sleeve at 50 000 CNY where the gate forces one of three funds; the numbers come from the base-regime grid priced in evidence/probe-constraint-control and re-confirmed in evidence/probe-sleeve-dispersion. Holds for the six recorded starts only.
minority: Prefer a return-based rule (trailing 252-session return) that would also have picked 513100 at 5/6 starts, on the grounds that a rule generalises where a name does not; rejected because that rule's success here is indistinguishable from having picked the winning index, and the rule would silently switch funds when the past decade reverses.
data.remainingRisk: The named index is the decade's winner; a specification that hardens it captures an exposure choice whose future is unknown, and the equity sleeve's near-zero CAGRs are the standing warning that this book's returns are not mainly a construction question.
data.verifyPlan: Run the engine with SLEEVE_MEMBERS['overseas'] = ('513100',) at every recorded start and confirm it reproduces the 513100-first cell terminal NAV exactly (a one-member tuple is order-free, so any difference would be a routing artefact).
data.reopenCondition: Evidence that the overseas sleeve can hold two funds inside the 50-100k range, or a mandate change that moves the sleeve weight.
